summary: Target-level plan of the random Γ-group theory of Liu–Wood–Zureick-Brown, Part I, with the Liu–Wood (2020) lemmas it rests on, as a Part II of ArithmeticStatistics. RG.0 fixes Γ-groups, the map Y, the coprime conjugacy hypothesis (SZ_Γ), sections and admissibility (importing the definition of admissibility and profinite complements from InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.4). RG.1 builds level-𝒞 completions (not the extension-closed pro-C completion), the free pro-|Γ|′ Γ-group F_n(Γ), the free admissible Γ-group 𝓕_n with its universal property, and Property E at a level with the criterion of Proposition 3.13. RG.2 defines the space 𝒫 with its basic opens and the random groups X_{u,n} with laws μ_{u,n}. RG.3 proves the exact finite-level distribution (Theorem 4.12) through products of irreducible operator groups, the fundamental sequence, H-extensions with their Möbius function and the λ-invariants. RG.4 proves no escape of mass through chief factor pairs and the interchange lemma, constructs μ_u and μ_Γ, and proves weak convergence (Theorem 1.2) and the values on V_{𝒞,H} (Theorem 5.15). RG.5 computes the moments [A : A^Γ]^{−u} and the Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet and Boston–Bush–Hajir specializations; RG.6 states the conjecture as a proposition, its consistency with the Galois side, the comparison with ArithmeticStatistics ST.5's function-field moment theorem, and the occurrence of p-class tower groups in the model. The explicit limit formulas carry the Property E hypothesis their printed versions omit; every statement using complement conjugacy carries (SZ_Γ), recorded as a Feit–Thompson gap for non-solvable Γ. The three other Part II directions of the job are proposed as separate roadmaps.

nodes.title: Γ-groups and their equivariant maps
nodes.statement: Let Γ be a finite group. A Γ-group is a profinite group G (a compact, Hausdorff, totally disconnected topological group) with an action of Γ on G by continuous group automorphisms; as Γ is finite and discrete, the action map Γ × G → G is then continuous. A morphism of Γ-groups is a continuous Γ-equivariant homomorphism; Hom_Γ(G, H), Sur_Γ(G, H) and Aut_Γ(G) denote the morphisms, the surjective morphisms and the automorphisms. A Γ-subgroup is a closed Γ-stable subgroup; a Γ-quotient is the target of a surjective morphism. For S ⊆ G, [S]_G is the smallest closed normal Γ-subgroup of G containing S, and G is Γ-generated by S when the closed subgroup generated by {γ(s) : γ ∈ Γ, s ∈ S} is G. G is an irreducible Γ-group when it is non-trivial and its only closed normal Γ-subgroups are 1 and G (for an action that contains the inner automorphisms, every Γ-stable subgroup is normal and the condition reads: no proper non-trivial Γ-subgroups). For finite H, h_Γ(H) = |Hom_Γ(H, H)|. G^Γ is the closed subgroup of Γ-fixed points and H ⋊ Γ the semidirect product for the action. For a positive integer n, G is an n′-Γ-group (pro-n′) when every quotient of G by an open normal subgroup has order prime to n, equivalently when the supernatural order of G is prime to n. The same vocabulary is used for an arbitrary group F acting on a finite group (an F-group), as in Liu–Wood §2.2.
hypotheses: Γ is a finite group; groups acted on are profinite (finite groups carry the discrete topology).
proofSteps: Model a Γ-group as a profinite group with Mathlib's MulDistribMulAction Γ G and continuity of each γ (ContinuousConstSMul); continuity of the joint action follows because Γ is finite and discrete.
Model morphisms as continuous elements of Mathlib's MulDistribMulActionHom G →*[Γ] H; Sur_Γ and Aut_Γ are the surjective and invertible ones.
Define [S]_G as the topological closure of the normal closure of the Γ-orbit of S; it is Γ-stable because Γ acts by continuous automorphisms that preserve normal closures and closures.
Define pro-n′ through the quotients by open normal subgroups and identify it with coprimality of TauCeti.profiniteOrder with n (Ribes–Zalesskii §2.3, the supernatural order).
The semidirect product H ⋊ Γ is Mathlib's SemidirectProduct for the homomorphism Γ → MulAut H given by the action.
acceptance: For Γ = 1 the notions are those of profinite groups and their continuous homomorphisms.
Γ-equivariant homomorphisms G → H correspond to homomorphisms G ⋊ Γ → H ⋊ Γ over Γ that are the identity on Γ.

nodes.title: The map Y
nodes.statement: Fix a tuple (γ_1, …, γ_d) of generators of Γ. For a Γ-group G define Y : G → G^d by Y(g) = (g⁻¹γ_1(g), …, g⁻¹γ_d(g)), write Y(G) for its image, and for S ⊆ G write [Y(S)] for the closed normal Γ-subgroup generated by the coordinates of the Y(s), s ∈ S. Y is continuous, Y(1) = 1, Y(gh) = h⁻¹Y(g)h · Y(h) coordinatewise, and Y(g) = Y(h) iff hg⁻¹ ∈ G^Γ; hence the fibres of Y are the right cosets G^Γ g, the partition of G into fibres does not depend on the generating tuple, and for finite G, |G| = |G^Γ| · |Y(G)| (LWZB Lemma 3.5). Morphisms commute with Y. Using all elements of Γ as the tuple, Y(g) is the principal crossed homomorphism σ ↦ g⁻¹σ(g).
hypotheses: (γ_1, …, γ_d) generates Γ; G is a Γ-group.
proofSteps: h⁻¹γ(h) = g⁻¹γ(g) is equivalent to γ(hg⁻¹) = hg⁻¹; quantifying over the generators gives hg⁻¹ ∈ G^Γ, because a generating tuple fixes an element iff Γ does.
The fibre through g is therefore the right coset G^Γ g, which gives |G| = |G^Γ||Y(G)| for finite G (LWZB Lemma 3.5).
Twisted multiplicativity: (gh)⁻¹γ(gh) = h⁻¹(g⁻¹γ(g))h · h⁻¹γ(h).
Naturality: φ(g)⁻¹γ(φ(g)) = φ(g⁻¹γ(g)) for a Γ-equivariant homomorphism φ.
acceptance: The fibre partition is the same for every generating tuple (the criterion hg⁻¹ ∈ G^Γ does not mention the tuple), which is the content of LWZB Lemma 3.9's independence statement at the level of sets.

Introduces the notation [Y(S)] for the closed normal Γ-subgroup generated by the coordinates of Y(r), r ∈ S.

nodes.title: The coprime conjugacy hypothesis (SZ)
nodes.statement: For a finite group Γ, (SZ_Γ) is the proposition: for every finite group N of order prime to |Γ| with an action of Γ by automorphisms, every crossed homomorphism c : Γ → N (c(στ) = c(σ)·σ(c(τ))) is principal, c(σ) = g⁻¹σ(g) for some g ∈ N; equivalently the non-abelian H¹(Γ, N) is a point; equivalently all complements of N in N ⋊ Γ are N-conjugate. (SZ_Γ) holds when Γ is solvable, and for each abelian N without hypothesis on Γ; for all Γ it is equivalent, given Schur–Zassenhaus existence, to the conjugacy half of the Schur–Zassenhaus theorem, whose proof in general uses the Feit–Thompson theorem. A profinite version follows by compactness: if (SZ_Γ) holds then for every |Γ|′-Γ-group N every continuous crossed homomorphism Γ → N is principal.
hypotheses: Γ finite; N finite (respectively pro-|Γ|′ for the profinite form) with gcd(|N|, |Γ|) = 1.
proofSteps: Crossed homomorphisms c correspond to sections σ ↦ (c(σ), σ) of N ⋊ Γ → Γ, principal ones to the N-conjugates of the trivial section; this gives the equivalence of the three formulations.
Abelian N: Mathlib's Subgroup.exists_smul_eq (the abelian Schur–Zassenhaus conjugacy) and ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/complements-of-a-coprime-abelian-normal-subgroup-are-conjugate.

Solvable Γ: the classical induction on |N ⋊ Γ| over a minimal normal subgroup of the solvable complement (Gorenstein, Finite Groups, Theorem 6.2.1, case of a solvable quotient), using the abelian case at each step.

General Γ: one of |N|, |Γ| is odd, hence the corresponding group is solvable by Feit–Thompson, and the solvable cases apply. Neither library nor any atlas layer has Feit–Thompson; this is recorded as a gap.

Profinite form: the sets of g ∈ N/U trivializing c mod U are non-empty finite and compatible over the open normal Γ-stable U, so their inverse limit is non-empty (as in InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.4/coprime-profinite-complements).
acceptance: (SZ_Γ) holds for Γ = Z/2, Z/4, (Z/2)², D_8 and S_3, which covers every Γ in the test cases of RG.5.
Dropping coprimality breaks it: Γ = Z/2 acting trivially on N = Z/2 has the non-principal crossed homomorphism id : Γ → N.

sources.locator: §2, p. 10, and the proof of Lemma 3.6, p. 14

Notes that for |Γ| odd the random groups need not be prosolvable, so the conjugacy input is not covered by a solvability argument on the side of the random group.

nodes.title: Sections of G ⋊ Γ and the fibres of Y (Lemmas 3.4–3.6)
nodes.statement: Assume (SZ_Γ). (a) For a |Γ|′-Γ-group G, sending g to the g-conjugate of the trivial section induces a bijection between Y(G) and the continuous sections of G ⋊ Γ → Γ; the sections form one G-conjugacy class with stabilizer G^Γ. (b) (Lemma 3.4) For a closed Γ-subgroup E of a |Γ|′-Γ-group G, Y(E) = Y(G) ∩ E^d. (c) (Lemma 3.6) For an exact sequence 1 → N → G → H → 1 of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups: 1 → N^Γ → G^Γ → H^Γ → 1 is exact; |Y(N)| = |Y(G)|/|Y(H)|; and |Y(G) ∩ π⁻¹(x)| = |Y(G)|/|Y(H)| for every x ∈ Y(H), where π also denotes G^d → H^d.
hypotheses: (SZ_Γ) (RG.0/coprime-conjugacy-hypothesis), or the special case it covers (Γ solvable, or all groups involved abelian)
G, E, N, G, H are pro-|Γ|′ (finite in (c))
proofSteps: (a) Conjugating the trivial section by (g, 1) gives γ_i ↦ (g⁻¹γ_i(g), γ_i); two such agree on the generators iff they agree everywhere, so the induced map from Y(G) is injective; surjectivity is (SZ_Γ) in its profinite form.
(b) A section with image in E ⋊ Γ is a section of E ⋊ Γ → Γ, and conversely; apply (a) to E and to G.
(c) The long exact sequence of pointed sets 1 → N^Γ → G^Γ → H^Γ → H¹(Γ, N) has H¹(Γ, N) = 1 by (SZ_Γ), giving exactness; with RG.0/y-map (|X| = |X^Γ||Y(X)|) this gives |Y(N)| = |Y(G)|/|Y(H)|.
For the fibre count, fix g over h with Y(h) = x; z ↦ (g, …, g)·z·(γ_1(g)⁻¹, …, γ_d(g)⁻¹) preserves Y(G) and carries π⁻¹(x) onto N^d, so each fibre has |Y(G) ∩ N^d| = |Y(N)| elements by (b).

nodes.title: Admissible Γ-groups: closure properties and the abelian criterion
nodes.statement: Call a Γ-group admissible when it is pro-|Γ|′ and topologically generated by {g⁻¹γ(g) : g ∈ G, γ ∈ Γ} (the definition of InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.4/unramified-gamma-groups). Then: (a) Γ-quotients and finite products of admissible Γ-groups are admissible; (b) (Lemma 3.9) an admissible G is Γ-generated by the coordinates of Y(G) for any generating tuple of Γ; (c) (Lemma 3.12) if G̃ is admissible and N a closed normal Γ-subgroup on which Γ acts trivially, then N is central in G̃; (d) (rigidity) if E is admissible and D a closed Γ-subgroup with Y(D) = Y(E), then D = E; (e) (§7.1) a finite abelian |Γ|′-Γ-group H is admissible iff H^Γ = 1; (f) the Γ-coinvariants G/[g⁻¹γ(g)] of an admissible G are trivial, and an admissible Γ-group has no non-trivial Γ-quotient with trivial Γ-action.
hypotheses: Γ finite; for (e) the hypothesis (SZ_Γ) is not needed because H is abelian.
proofSteps: (a) A surjection carries the generators g⁻¹γ(g) onto generators of the same form; for products use the coordinates.
(b) Expand g⁻¹σ(g) for σ = σ_1⋯σ_s a word in the generators as the product of σ_1⋯σ_{k−1}(g⁻¹σ_k(g)), each factor a Γ-translate of a coordinate of Y(g).
(c) For n ∈ N: (g⁻¹γ(g)) n (g⁻¹γ(g))⁻¹ = g⁻¹γ(g n g⁻¹)g = n because Γ fixes g n g⁻¹ ∈ N; the generators of G̃ centralize N, hence G̃ does.
(d) By (b), E is generated by the Γ-translates of the coordinates of Y(E) = Y(D) ⊆ D^d, and D is a Γ-subgroup.

(e) As |H| is prime to |Γ|, e = |Γ|⁻¹Σ_γ γ is an idempotent endomorphism of H with image H^Γ, and x − e(x) = |Γ|⁻¹Σ_γ (x − γx) lies in the subgroup S generated by the (γ − 1)h, while e kills S. Hence H = H^Γ ⊕ S, so H = S (admissible) iff H^Γ = 0. This is the additive form of the argument of §7.1, which uses Lemma 3.6(1).
(f) The coinvariant quotient has trivial Γ-action, so all g⁻¹γ(g) lie in the kernel, which is therefore everything.
acceptance: Γ = Z/2: Z/3 with inversion is admissible, Z/3 with trivial action is not (its Y-image is trivial).
Γ = Z/3 acting on (Z/2)² through multiplication by a primitive cube root of unity in F_4 is admissible (no non-zero fixed vector).

nodes.title: Level-𝒞 closure and the pro-𝒞 completion of a Γ-group
nodes.statement: For a set 𝒞 of (isomorphism classes of) finite Γ-groups let 𝒞̄ be the smallest set of isomorphism classes of finite Γ-groups containing 𝒞 and closed under finite direct products, Γ-subgroups and Γ-quotients. For a Γ-group G, its pro-𝒞 completion is G^𝒞 = lim_M G/M over the closed normal Γ-subgroups M of G with G/M ∈ 𝒞̄ (LWZB (3.11)), with the canonical surjection η : G → G^𝒞; G is of level 𝒞 when η is an isomorphism. For ℓ ≥ 1, 𝒞_ℓ is the set of |Γ|′-Γ-groups of order at most ℓ. The construction is a functor from Γ-groups to Γ-groups of level 𝒞, left adjoint to the inclusion: every morphism from G to a Γ-group of level 𝒞 factors uniquely through η. It preserves surjections; ker η is the intersection of the M above; (G^𝒞)^𝒟 = G^𝒟 when 𝒟̄ ⊆ 𝒞̄; a finite Γ-group lies in 𝒞̄ iff it is of level 𝒞. 𝒞̄ need not be closed under extensions, so for most 𝒞 (groups of bounded order, groups of bounded p-class) this is not the pro-C completion of an extension-closed class.
hypotheses: 𝒞 a set of finite Γ-groups; G a Γ-group.
proofSteps: The family of M with G/M ∈ 𝒞̄ is closed under finite intersections, because G/(M ∩ M′) embeds Γ-equivariantly in G/M × G/M′ and 𝒞̄ is closed under products and Γ-subgroups; so the inverse limit is over a directed system of finite Γ-quotients.
The limit of the finite discrete quotients is profinite with the induced Γ-action; η is surjective by compactness (an inverse limit of surjections of compact Hausdorff groups).

Universal property: a morphism f : G → L with L of level 𝒞 has, for each M_L with L/M_L ∈ 𝒞̄, preimage M = f⁻¹(M_L) with G/M ↪ L/M_L, hence G/M ∈ 𝒞̄; the compatible maps G/M → L/M_L assemble to G^𝒞 → L^𝒞 = L.
Surjections are preserved: for f : F → H surjective, the image of F^𝒞 → H^𝒞 is closed and dense (LWZB, the standard argument after (3.11)).

For 𝒞 the class of all finite p-Γ-groups (p ∤ |Γ|) the completion is the maximal pro-p quotient TauCeti.maximalProPQuotient with its induced action, because that class is closed under extensions as well.
acceptance: Every Γ-group of level 𝒞 is pro-𝒞̄ and every finite member of 𝒞̄ is of level 𝒞.
For 𝒞 ⊆ 𝒞_ℓ, U_{𝒞,H} is a union of the sets U_{𝒞_ℓ,H′} (used in RG.2).

The Γ = 1 version: the variety generated by S and the pro-S̄ completion; for profinite G in 𝒫, G is of level S iff G = G^S̄.

nodes.title: The free pro-|Γ|′ Γ-group F_n(Γ)
nodes.statement: For n ≥ 0, F_n(Γ) is the free pro-|Γ|′ group on the finite set {x_{i,γ} : 1 ≤ i ≤ n, γ ∈ Γ} (the free pro-C group for the extension-closed class C of finite groups of order prime to |Γ|), with σ ∈ Γ acting by the automorphism induced by the permutation x_{i,γ} ↦ x_{i,σγ} of the basis. Put x_i = x_{i,1}. Universal property: for every |Γ|′-Γ-group G and g_1, …, g_n ∈ G there is a unique morphism of Γ-groups F_n(Γ) → G with x_i ↦ g_i (then x_{i,γ} ↦ γ(g_i)). Its abelianization is (Ẑ′[Γ])^n with Ẑ′ = ∏_{p∤|Γ|} Z_p.
hypotheses: n ≥ 0; Γ finite.
proofSteps: Take the free pro-C group of tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 4 for C the finite groups of order prime to |Γ|, a class closed under subgroups, quotients and extensions.
Functoriality of the free object in its basis gives an action of the symmetric group of {1..n} × Γ, which restricts to Γ acting on the second coordinate by left multiplication.
The equivariant universal property is the plain universal property applied to x_{i,γ} ↦ γ(g_i), whose equivariance is checked on the basis.
The abelianization is the free pro-|Γ|′ abelian group on the basis, i.e. (Ẑ′)^{n|Γ|} = Ẑ′[Γ]^n as a Γ-module.
acceptance: F_0(Γ) is trivial; for Γ = 1, F_n(1) is the free profinite group on n generators.

nodes.title: The free admissible Γ-group 𝓕_n (Lemma 3.1, Remark 3.2)
nodes.statement: 𝓕_n = 𝓕_n(Γ) is the closed Γ-subgroup of F_n(Γ) generated by the elements x_i⁻¹γ_j(x_i) (1 ≤ i ≤ n, 1 ≤ j ≤ d). Under (SZ_Γ): (Lemma 3.1) 𝓕_n is admissible, and there is a surjective morphism of Γ-groups π : F_n(Γ) → 𝓕_n with π ∘ ι = id, where ι is the inclusion and π(x_i) = y_i for elements y_i ∈ 𝓕_n with Y(y_i) = Y(x_i); (Remark 3.2) as a pro-|Γ|′ group 𝓕_n is free on {x_i⁻¹σ(x_i) : 1 ≤ i ≤ n, σ ∈ Γ ∖ 1}, it is Γ-generated by n elements, and every pro-|Γ|′ Γ-group generated by elements h_i⁻¹γ(h_i) (1 ≤ i ≤ n, γ ∈ Γ) is a Γ-quotient of 𝓕_n. 𝓕_n does not depend on the generating tuple (Lemma 3.9).
hypotheses: (SZ_Γ) for the retraction and for admissibility; n ≥ 1.
proofSteps: The x_i⁻¹γ(x_i) for all γ lie in 𝓕_n (RG.0/admissible-gamma-groups(b) expansion), so 𝓕_n contains every x_i⁻¹σ(x_i).

Freeness (Remark 3.2(1)): after the change of basis x_{i,σ} ↦ x_i⁻¹x_{i,σ} (σ ≠ 1) of F_n, the elements x_i⁻¹σ(x_i) are part of a basis, and the closed subgroup they generate is Γ-stable because σ(x_i⁻¹τ(x_i)) = (x_i⁻¹σ(x_i))⁻¹(x_i⁻¹στ(x_i)).

Lemma 3.1: by RG.0/sections-and-y(b) with G = F_n and E = 𝓕_n, Y(x_i) ∈ Y(F_n) ∩ 𝓕_n^d = Y(𝓕_n), so y_i exists; comparing coordinates shows that 𝓕_n is generated by the y_i⁻¹γ(y_i), i.e. admissible; π is the morphism x_i ↦ y_i, and π ∘ ι = id because both fix the generators x_i⁻¹γ_j(x_i) = y_i⁻¹γ_j(y_i).
Remark 3.2(3): x_i ↦ h_i defines F_n → H, whose restriction to 𝓕_n is onto because H is generated by the h_i⁻¹γ(h_i).
acceptance: For Γ = Z/2 = ⟨σ⟩, 𝓕_1 is procyclic on y = x⁻¹σ(x) with σ(y) = y⁻¹, so 𝓕_1 ≅ Ẑ_odd with σ = −1.
𝓕_n is never F_n for Γ ≠ 1 and n ≥ 1: x_1 ∉ 𝓕_n.

nodes.title: Homomorphisms out of 𝓕_n (Corollary 3.8, Corollary 3.10, finiteness)
nodes.statement: Assume (SZ_Γ). (a) (Corollary 3.8) For every pro-|Γ|′ Γ-group G, the map Y(G)^n → Hom_Γ(𝓕_n, G) sending (Y(g_1), …, Y(g_n)) to the restriction to 𝓕_n of the morphism F_n → G with x_i ↦ g_i is well defined and bijective. (b) Consequently |Hom_Γ(𝓕_n, H)| = [H : H^Γ]^n for finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups H, and for finite admissible H, |Sur_Γ(𝓕_n, H)|·[H : H^Γ]^{−n} ≤ 1 and → 1 as n → ∞ (LWZB (4.18)). (c) For a set 𝒞 of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups and finite H of level 𝒞, morphisms (𝓕_n)^𝒞 → H correspond to morphisms 𝓕_n → H, hence to Y(H)^n. (d) (Corollary 3.10) 𝓕_n^ab ≅ (Ẑ′[Γ]/(Σ_{g∈Γ} g))^n as Γ-modules, with Ẑ′ = ∏_{p∤|Γ|} Z_p, and (𝓕_n^ab)^Γ = 0. (e) For finite 𝒞, (𝓕_n)^𝒞 is finite.
hypotheses: (SZ_Γ); G pro-|Γ|′ in (a) — the statement fails for Γ = Z/2 acting on Z/4 by inversion.
proofSteps: (a) Injectivity: two maps x_i ↦ g_i, g_i′ agree on 𝓕_n iff they agree on the generators x_i⁻¹γ_j(x_i), i.e. iff Y(g_i) = Y(g_i′). Surjectivity: extend a morphism 𝓕_n → G along the retraction π of RG.1/free-admissible-gamma-group.

(b) RG.0/y-map gives |Y(H)| = [H : H^Γ]; non-surjective morphisms land in proper Γ-subgroups H′, each with |Y(H′)| < |Y(H)| by RG.0/admissible-gamma-groups(d), so their number is at most Σ_{H′} |Y(H′)|^n = o(|Y(H)|^n).
(c) Universal property of the level-𝒞 completion (RG.1/level-completion).

(d) 𝓕_n^ab injects into F_n^ab = Ẑ′[Γ]^n (if [x, y] ∈ F_n with x, y ∈ 𝓕_n then [x, y] = π([x, y]) ∈ [𝓕_n, 𝓕_n]) with image I^n, I the augmentation ideal; |Γ| is invertible in Ẑ′ so Ẑ′[Γ] = I ⊕ Ẑ′·Σg and I ≅ Ẑ′[Γ]/(Σg); I^Γ = 0 because |Γ|⁻¹Σg acts as 0 on I.
(e) The intersection W of the kernels of the finitely many Γ-maps from 𝓕_n to members of 𝒞 has finite index and is killed by all maps to 𝒞̄ (lift maps to quotients by π), so (𝓕_n)^𝒞 = 𝓕_n/W.

nodes.title: Property E relative to a level: restriction and completion
nodes.statement: Property E is taken in the general form of LWZB Definition 2.3: for a full subcategory 𝒦 of Γ-groups, H ∈ 𝒦 has Property E for 𝒦 if every Γ-surjection H → G lifts to a Γ-surjection H → G̃ along every non-split central extension 1 → Z/p → G̃ → G → 1 in 𝒦 with trivial Γ-action on Z/p (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.4/property-e, which states it for 𝒦 the pro-Δ′ Γ-groups). For a set 𝒞 of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups, 'Property E at level 𝒞' means Property E for the Γ-groups of level 𝒞. Then: (a) if 𝒦′ ⊆ 𝒦 are full subcategories and H ∈ 𝒦′ has Property E for 𝒦, it has Property E for 𝒦′; (b) if a Γ-group X has Property E for a full subcategory containing all Γ-groups of level 𝒞 and X itself, then X^𝒞 has Property E at level 𝒞; (c) for p ∤ |Γ| and X with Property E for the pro-p Γ-groups, X^𝒞 has Property E at level 𝒞 for every set 𝒞 of finite p-Γ-groups; (d) for finite H it suffices to test extensions G̃ of finite Γ-groups G that are Γ-quotients of H, and every lift H → G̃ of a surjection whose composite with G̃ → G is onto is itself onto (a weak lift is proper).
hypotheses: Full subcategories closed under isomorphism; extensions tested inside the subcategory.
proofSteps: (a) Fewer extensions are tested in 𝒦′.

(b) Given a Γ-surjection X^𝒞 → G and a non-split central G̃ → G of level 𝒞, compose with η : X → X^𝒞, lift to X → G̃ by Property E of X, and factor through X^𝒞 because G̃ is of level 𝒞 (RG.1/level-completion).
(c) The level-𝒞 groups for a set of p-Γ-groups are pro-p, so (b) applies with the pro-p subcategory.
(d) A lift H → G̃ whose image maps onto G either is onto or has image meeting Z/p trivially, which would split the extension over G.
acceptance: Γ = Z/2, p = 3, H = F_3² with σ = −1 lacks Property E at the level of 3-Γ-groups of 3-class ≤ 2: the Heisenberg group of order 27 with σ acting by −1 on generators (hence trivially on the centre) is a non-split central extension, and |H| = 9 < 27.
Γ = Z/3, H = (Z/2)² with a nontrivial Z/3-action is admissible but lacks Property E for any level containing Q_8 with its compatible Z/3-action, since |H| = 4 < 8.

nodes.title: Property E as the shape of the relations (Proposition 3.13)
nodes.statement: Assume (SZ_Γ). Let n ≥ 1, 𝒞 a set of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups and φ : (𝓕_n)^𝒞 → H a Γ-surjection. Then ker φ = [Y(ker φ)] (the closed normal Γ-subgroup of (𝓕_n)^𝒞 generated by the coordinates of Y(ker φ)) iff H has Property E at level 𝒞. In particular, for every S ⊆ 𝓕_n the group (𝓕_n)^𝒞/[Y(S)] — and so every (X_{u,n})^𝒞 of RG.2 — has Property E at level 𝒞.
hypotheses: (SZ_Γ); 𝒞 consists of |Γ|′-groups so that RG.0/sections-and-y applies to the kernels.
proofSteps: (⇒) Let θ : H → G be a Γ-surjection with a non-split central extension G̃ → G of level 𝒞, and ϖ = θ ∘ φ. Choose g̃_i ∈ G̃ over ϖ(π(x_i)); non-splitness makes G̃ Γ-generated by the g̃_i⁻¹γ_j(g̃_i), giving a surjection ρ : (𝓕_n)^𝒞 → G̃ over ϖ.

From 1 → ker ρ → ker ϖ → Z/p → 1 with |Y(Z/p)| = 1 (trivial action) and Lemma 3.4: Y(ker φ) ⊆ Y((𝓕_n)^𝒞) ∩ (ker ϖ)^d = Y(ker ϖ) = Y(ker ρ) ⊆ (ker ρ)^d; so ρ factors through (𝓕_n)^𝒞/[Y(ker φ)] = H. (The printed proof applies the finite-group Lemma 3.6(2) to the possibly infinite ker ϖ; the containment argument via Lemma 3.4 avoids it, source issue E3 here.)
(⇐) If [Y(ker φ)] ⊊ ker φ, put M = ker φ/[Y(ker φ)] and E = (𝓕_n)^𝒞/[Y(ker φ)]. Γ acts trivially on M, E is admissible, so E centralizes M (RG.0/admissible-gamma-groups(c)).

A maximal proper subgroup D of M gives 1 → N → H̃ → H → 1 with N = M/D simple, central, hence Z/p with trivial action; it is split only if H̃ = N × H, contradicting admissibility of H̃, and non-split contradicts Property E of H.
acceptance: For Γ = Z/3 and H = (Z/2)² with nontrivial action, the kernel of any surjection (𝓕_1)^𝒞 → H, 𝒞 ∋ Q_8, is not generated by Y-relations, matching the failure of Property E.
For abelian 𝒞 and H with H^Γ = 1 every Γ-quotient has Property E at level 𝒞 (no non-split central extensions of level 𝒞 exist by abelianness), consistent with §7.1.

nodes.title: The space 𝒫 of admissible Γ-groups
nodes.statement: 𝒫 = 𝒫_Γ is the set of isomorphism classes of admissible |Γ|′-Γ-groups X such that X^𝒞 is finite for every finite set 𝒞 of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups. For such 𝒞 and a finite |Γ|′-Γ-group H, the basic open set is U_{𝒞,H} = {X ∈ 𝒫 : X^𝒞 ≅ H}; 𝒫 carries the topology generated by these sets, its Borel σ-algebra, the algebra 𝒜 of sets generated by the basic opens, and, for an arbitrary set 𝒞, the sets V_{𝒞,H} = {X : X^𝒞 ≅ H}. Facts: U_{𝒞,H} = ∅ unless H is of level 𝒞; for each ℓ, the sets U_{𝒞_ℓ,H} (H of level 𝒞_ℓ) are pairwise disjoint and cover 𝒫, and each U_{𝒞,H} with 𝒞 ⊆ 𝒞_ℓ is a union of them; the level-tower map X ↦ ([X^{𝒞_ℓ}])_{ℓ≥1} is injective, so 𝒫 is a set and its topology is the subspace topology from a countable product of countable discrete sets — in particular second countable and Hausdorff, every open set is a countable disjoint union of basic opens, and V_{𝒞,H} = ⋂_i U_{𝒟_i,H} for any exhaustion 𝒟_1 ⊆ 𝒟_2 ⊆ ⋯ of 𝒞 by finite sets with H of level 𝒟_i.
hypotheses: Γ finite; isomorphism classes of finite Γ-groups of bounded order form a finite set.
proofSteps: Each X ∈ 𝒫 is the inverse limit of its completions X^{𝒞_ℓ}, since every open normal subgroup contains an open normal Γ-stable one (intersect the finitely many Γ-translates) and so every finite Γ-quotient of X has level 𝒞_ℓ for some ℓ.

Injectivity of the tower map: if X^{𝒞_ℓ} ≅ X′^{𝒞_ℓ} for all ℓ, the sets of isomorphisms at level ℓ are finite, non-empty and form an inverse system under the completion maps (RG.1/level-completion), so a compatible system of isomorphisms exists and X ≅ X′.
For 𝒞 ⊆ 𝒞_ℓ, X^𝒞 = (X^{𝒞_ℓ})^𝒞, so U_{𝒞,H} is the union of U_{𝒞_ℓ,H′} over the level-𝒞_ℓ classes H′ with H′^𝒞 ≅ H; the level-ℓ sets are disjoint because X^{𝒞_ℓ} has one class.
Countability: there are countably many pairs (𝒞, H) up to isomorphism; an open set is the union of the level sets it contains, and refining to a common level gives a countable disjoint union.
acceptance: For Γ = 1 an admissible group is generated by elements g⁻¹g = 1, so 𝒫 is a single point.
The trivial class lies in U_{𝒞_ℓ,1} for every ℓ and {[1]} = ⋂_ℓ U_{𝒞_ℓ,1} = V_{all,1}.

nodes.title: Random Γ-groups X_{u,n} and their laws μ_{u,n} (Definition 3.15)
nodes.statement: For n ≥ 1 and an integer u > −n, let S = (s_1, …, s_{n+u}) be distributed by the product of n + u copies of the Haar probability measure of the compact group 𝓕_n (TauCeti.haarProb), and put X_{u,n} = 𝓕_n/[Y(S)] (u = 1 by default: X_{Γ,n} = X_{1,n}). Its law μ_{u,n} is the Borel probability measure on 𝒫 with μ_{u,n}(A) = Prob([X_{u,n}] ∈ A). For finite 𝒞, (X_{u,n})^𝒞 ≅ (𝓕_n)^𝒞/[Y(S̄)] with S̄ the image of S in the finite group (𝓕_n)^𝒞, and the image of Haar measure is the uniform measure; so μ_{u,n}(U_{𝒞,H}) = Prob((𝓕_n)^𝒞/[Y(r_1, …, r_{n+u})] ≅ H) for independent uniform r_j ∈ (𝓕_n)^𝒞. Every (X_{u,n})^𝒞 has Property E at level 𝒞. The measures μ_u on 𝒜 are the limits μ_u(A) = lim_n μ_{u,n}(A), whose existence is RG.3 and whose extension is RG.4.
hypotheses: (SZ_Γ) (through RG.1); n ≥ 1, u > −n.
proofSteps: X_{u,n} is admissible (a Γ-quotient of 𝓕_n) and its level-𝒞 completions are quotients of the finite (𝓕_n)^𝒞, so [X_{u,n}] ∈ 𝒫.
Completion commutes with the quotient: (𝓕_n/[Y(S)])^𝒞 = (𝓕_n)^𝒞/[Y(S̄)] by the universal property, since a map to a level-𝒞 group killing Y(S) factors through (𝓕_n)^𝒞.

The pushforward of Haar probability along a continuous surjection onto a finite group is uniform (invariance plus uniqueness, TauCeti.haarProb_eq_uniformOn_univ and Mathlib's uniqueness of Haar probability measures).

Measurability: each event {X^𝒞 ≅ H} is a union of fibres of S ↦ S̄, hence clopen in 𝓕_n^{n+u}; the basic opens generate the Borel σ-algebra (RG.2/space-of-admissible-gamma-groups), so S ↦ [X_{u,n}] is measurable.
Property E: RG.1/property-e-criterion applied to (𝓕_n)^𝒞 → (𝓕_n)^𝒞/[Y(S̄)].
acceptance: Γ = Z/2, n = 1, u = 0: 𝓕_1 ≅ Ẑ_odd with σ = −1 and Y(r) = −2r, so X_{0,1} ≅ Ẑ_odd/rẐ_odd and Prob(3 ∤ |X_{0,1}|) = Prob(r ∈ Z_3^×) = 2/3.

nodes.title: Products of irreducible F-groups (Liu–Wood §§5–7)
nodes.statement: Let F be a group and G_1, …, G_k pairwise non-isomorphic finite irreducible F-groups, R = ∏ G_i^{m_i}. (a) (Liu–Wood Lemmas 5.3–5.5, Corollary 5.6) every normal F-subgroup of R is ∏ N_i with N_i a normal F-subgroup of G_i^{m_i}, and it is R iff each projection to G_i^{m_i} is onto. (b) (Lemma 5.8) for G non-abelian, a normal F-subgroup of G^m is G^m iff all m projections to G are non-trivial; for G abelian, iff its projection to the first m − 1 factors is onto and its projection to the last factor does not factor through that projection. (c) (Theorem 5.1) for N ≥ 1 independent uniform x_1, …, x_N ∈ R, Prob([x_1, …, x_N]_F = R) = ∏_{G_i abelian} ∏_{j=0}^{m_i−1}(1 − h_F(G_i)^j |G_i|^{−N}) ∏_{G_i non-abelian}(1 − |G_i|^{−N})^{m_i}. (d) (Theorem 7.1) |Sur_F(R, G_j)| = h_F(G_j)^{m_j} − 1 for G_j abelian and m_j·|Aut_F(G_j)| for G_j non-abelian. (e) (Lemma 5.11) for a finite group G, N ⊴ G and M the intersection of the maximal proper G-normal subgroups of N, N/M is, under conjugation, a product of irreducible G/M-groups, and its abelian factors are G/N-groups. (f) (Lemma 6.1) if (E, π) is an extension of a finite group H whose kernel G is a finite irreducible E-group, then G ≅ T^m for a finite simple group T and m ≤ |H|. (g) (Remark 5.2) for abelian irreducible G and m maximal such that G^m is F-generated by one element, h_F(G)^m = |G|.
hypotheses: F an arbitrary group acting by automorphisms; the G_i finite.
proofSteps: (a) A normal F-subgroup projecting to 1 or G_i in each coordinate is isomorphic to the product of a subset of the factors (Liu–Wood Lemma 5.3, induction on the number of factors); F-maps between non-isomorphic irreducibles with normal image are trivial (Lemma 5.4), which separates the isotypic parts (Lemma 5.5).
(b) Induction on m: πm(ker π) is 1 or G; if it were 1 then π would be injective on N and πm would factor through π, impossible for non-abelian G by a conjugation argument (Liu–Wood Lemma 5.8).

(c) Independence across isotypic parts (Corollary 5.7); for G^m condition on the first k projections: a bad choice of the (k+1)-st coordinates is one given by an F-map G^k → G, and there are h_F(G)^k of them (Corollaries 5.9–5.10).
(d) Restrict surjections to the factors and use (a) and Lemma 5.4 (Liu–Wood Lemmas 7.2–7.3).
(e) The maximal proper G-normal subgroups M_i of N give an embedding N/M ↪ ∏ (N/M)/M_i onto each factor; apply (a). On an abelian factor conjugation by N is trivial.
(f) For T = Z/p, H acts irreducibly on F_p^m so m ≤ |H|; for T non-abelian the normal copies of T are the factors and H permutes them transitively.
(g) Apply (c) with N = 1: the probability is positive for m_i = m and zero for m + 1.
acceptance: F = 1, G = Z/3: N ≥ m uniform vectors of F_3^m span with probability ∏_{j<m}(1 − 3^{j−N}); |Sur(F_3^m, Z/3)| = 3^m − 1.

nodes.title: The fundamental short exact sequence and the multiplicities m(𝒞, n, H, G)
nodes.statement: Let n ≥ 1, 𝒞 a finite set of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups, H a finite Γ-group of level 𝒞 and ϖ : (𝓕_n)^𝒞 → H a Γ-surjection with kernel N. Let M be the intersection of the maximal proper (𝓕_n)^𝒞-normal Γ-subgroups of N, F = (𝓕_n)^𝒞/M and R = N/M. The fundamental short exact sequence of (𝒞, n, ϖ) is 1 → R → F → H → 1 (LWZB (4.1)); it is induced by 1 → R → F ⋊ Γ → H ⋊ Γ → 1 (4.2), and R is a finite product of irreducible F ⋊ Γ-groups whose abelian factors are H ⋊ Γ-groups. 𝒜_H is the set of isomorphism classes of non-trivial finite abelian irreducible |Γ|′-(H ⋊ Γ)-groups — 'non-trivial' refers to the group, so Z/p with trivial action (p ∤ |Γ|) belongs to 𝒜_H, with |Y(Z/p)| = 1 — and 𝒩 the set of isomorphism classes of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups isomorphic as groups to T^j with T non-abelian simple. For G ∈ 𝒜_H, m(𝒞, n, ϖ, G) is the multiplicity of G in R as an H ⋊ Γ-group; for G ∈ 𝒩 it is the sum of the multiplicities in R of the irreducible F ⋊ Γ-group structures on G compatible with its Γ-action. These numbers depend only on (𝒞, n, H, G) (RG.3/multiplicities-via-extensions) and are non-zero for finitely many G.
hypotheses: 𝒞 finite, so (𝓕_n)^𝒞 is finite (RG.1/free-admissible-universal-property (e)).
proofSteps: Normal subgroups of (𝓕_n)^𝒞 ⋊ Γ contained in N are exactly the (𝓕_n)^𝒞-normal Γ-subgroups of N, so RG.3/products-of-irreducible-operator-groups (e) applies to N ⊴ (𝓕_n)^𝒞 ⋊ Γ and gives R as a product of irreducible F ⋊ Γ-groups.
Abelian factors: conjugation by R is trivial on them, so the F ⋊ Γ-action factors through H ⋊ Γ.

A subgroup of (𝓕_n)^𝒞 generated as a normal Γ-subgroup by elements of N equals N iff its image in F equals R, because a proper one would lie in a maximal proper (𝓕_n)^𝒞-normal Γ-subgroup of N (Liu–Wood §4, the argument before (4.2)).

Finiteness of the support: each irreducible factor is characteristically simple, hence a power of a simple group lying (as a group) in the subgroup-and-quotient closure of 𝒞 (Liu–Wood Corollary 6.12), with exponent at most |H ⋊ Γ| (part (f) of the products node).
acceptance: For a sufficiently large finite set 𝒞 of p-Γ-groups (Γ = Z/2, p odd, H with Y-generated relation kernel), the fundamental sequence is the p-covering-group sequence (LWZB Lemma 7.2, RG.5).

nodes.title: Generation by Y-relations (Proposition 4.3, Remark 4.4)
nodes.statement: Assume (SZ_Γ). Let F be a Γ-group, G_1, …, G_k pairwise non-isomorphic finite irreducible F ⋊ Γ-groups (of order prime to |Γ|) and R = ∏ G_i^{m_i}. For integers n, u with n + u ≥ 1 and r_1, …, r_{n+u} independent uniform elements of R, Prob([Y(r_1), …, Y(r_{n+u})]_{F⋊Γ} = R) = ∏_{G_i abelian} ∏_{j=0}^{m_i−1}(1 − h_{F⋊Γ}(G_i)^j |Y(G_i)|^{−n−u}) · ∏_{G_i non-abelian}(1 − |Y(G_i)|^{−n−u})^{m_i}, where [·]_{F⋊Γ} is the normal F ⋊ Γ-subgroup generated by the coordinates. (Remark 4.4) For an abelian irreducible F ⋊ Γ-group G and m maximal such that G^m is F ⋊ Γ-generated by the coordinates of one Y(g), h_{F⋊Γ}(G)^m = |Y(G)|.
hypotheses: (SZ_Γ) (for the count of maps in the abelian case, through Corollary 3.8)
the G_i of order prime to |Γ|
proofSteps: Normal F ⋊ Γ-subgroups of R split along the isotypic parts (RG.3/products-of-irreducible-operator-groups (a)), so the probability factors over the G_i^{m_i}.
Y(y) has all coordinates trivial iff y ∈ G^Γ, which for uniform y has probability |Y(G)|⁻¹ (RG.0/y-map).
Non-abelian G: by part (b) of the products node, G^m is generated iff each projection receives a non-trivial Y-coordinate, giving (1 − |Y(G)|^{−n−u})^m.

Abelian G: condition on the first m − 1 projections; the tuples Y(y_i) correspond to maps 𝓕_{n+u} → G^m (RG.1/free-admissible-universal-property (a)), and the bad last coordinates are those factoring through G^{m−1}: h_{F⋊Γ}(G)^{m−1} of the |Y(G)|^{n+u} possibilities (counted via RG.0/y-map). The printed proof writes 𝓕_n for 𝓕_{n+u} and Y[(…)] for [Y(…)] (source issue E11 here).
Remark 4.4: apply the formula with n + u = 1 for m and m + 1.
acceptance: Γ = Z/2, F = 1, R = (Z/3 with σ = −1)^m: the probability is ∏_{j<m}(1 − 3^{j−n−u}), the probability that n + u uniform vectors span F_3^m.
A factor Z/p with trivial action has |Y(Z/p)| = 1 and contributes the factor 1 − 1 = 0 when m ≥ 1: trivial-action factors are never generated by Y-relations.

sources.locator: Proposition 4.3 with proof and Remark 4.4, p. 21

nodes.title: H-extensions of Γ-groups and the Möbius function of sub-extensions
nodes.statement: For a Γ-group H, an H-extension is a pair (E, π) of a Γ-group E and a Γ-surjection π : E → H; a morphism (E, π) → (E′, π′) is a Γ-homomorphism f with π′ ∘ f = π, and Sur_{Γ,H}, Aut_{Γ,H} are the surjective morphisms and automorphisms. (E, π) is admissible if E is. A sub-H-extension of (E, π) is a closed Γ-subgroup E′ ≤ E with π(E′) = H; for finite E these form a finite poset 𝓔^E_H under inclusion with top element E, and ν(D, E) is its Möbius function: ν(E, E) = 1 and ν(D, E) = −Σ_{D ⊊ D′ ⊆ E} ν(D′, E) for D ≠ E (the printed recursion sums over all D′ ≠ D, source issue E5 here). For G ∈ 𝒜_H, 𝓔(G, H) is the set of isomorphism classes of admissible H-extensions with ker π ≅ G as H ⋊ Γ-groups (under conjugation); for G ∈ 𝒩, the admissible H-extensions with ker π ≅ G as Γ-groups and ker π an irreducible E ⋊ Γ-group. 𝓔_𝒞(G, H) ⊆ 𝓔(G, H) consists of those with E of level 𝒞; it is finite for finite 𝒞.
hypotheses: H a finite Γ-group; E finite for the poset and the Möbius function.
proofSteps: The Möbius function is Mathlib's IncidenceAlgebra.mu of the finite poset 𝓔^E_H, evaluated at (D, E).
Möbius inversion on 𝓔^E_H: if g(D) = Σ_{D′ ≤ D} f(D′) for every D, then f(E) = Σ_D ν(D, E) g(D).
Finiteness of 𝓔_𝒞(G, H): an extension of level 𝒞 is a Γ-quotient of a product of members of 𝒞 of bounded order |H||G|, and there are finitely many such up to isomorphism.
acceptance: The extension sets are the index sets of the sums (4.10)–(4.11) defining λ.

sources.locator: §4.1, pp. 21–22, before Lemma 4.6 and before Proposition 4.7
sources.match: Defines H-extensions of Γ-groups, admissible H-extensions, sub-H-extensions, the poset 𝓔^E_H with its Möbius function ν, and the sets 𝓔(G, H), 𝓔_𝒞(G, H) in the abelian and non-abelian cases.

nodes.title: Counting surjections of H-extensions (Lemma 4.6)
nodes.statement: Assume (SZ_Γ). Let n ≥ 1, 𝒞 a finite set of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups, H a finite Γ-group of level 𝒞, ρ : (𝓕_n)^𝒞 → H an H-extension structure and (E, π) a finite H-extension. Then |Sur_{Γ,H}(ρ, π)| = Σ_{D ∈ 𝓔^E_H} ν(D, E) (|Y(D)|/|Y(H)|)^n if E is admissible of level 𝒞, and 0 otherwise.
hypotheses: (SZ_Γ); all groups finite and pro-|Γ|′.
proofSteps: (𝓕_n)^𝒞 is admissible of level 𝒞, so its Γ-quotients are admissible of level 𝒞; this gives the vanishing case.

For a sub-H-extension D, morphisms (𝓕_n)^𝒞 → D over H correspond to elements of Y(D)^n lying over the element of Y(H)^n determined by ρ (RG.1/free-admissible-universal-property (a), (c)); by RG.0/sections-and-y (c) there are (|Y(D)|/|Y(H)|)^n of them.
Each such morphism is a surjection onto its image, a unique sub-H-extension D′ ≤ D: (|Y(D)|/|Y(H)|)^n = Σ_{D′ ≤ D} |Sur_{Γ,H}(ρ, D′)|.
Möbius inversion on 𝓔^E_H (RG.3/h-extensions).

sources.match: Counts surjections of H-extensions from (𝓕_n)^𝒞 by counting all maps into each sub-H-extension through Corollary 3.8 and Lemma 3.6(3), then inverting over the poset of sub-H-extensions.

nodes.title: Multiplicities through extensions (Proposition 4.7, Corollary 4.8, Remark 4.9)
nodes.statement: Assume (SZ_Γ). Let 1 → R → F → H → 1 be the fundamental sequence of (𝒞, n, ϖ) with H admissible. (1) For an irreducible abelian F ⋊ Γ-group G, |Sur_{F⋊Γ}(R, G)| = |Aut_{F⋊Γ}(G)| Σ_{(E,π)∈𝓔_𝒞(G,H)} Σ_{D∈𝓔^E_H} ν(D, E)(|Y(D)|/|Y(H)|)^n / |Aut_{Γ,H}(E, π)| when the F ⋊ Γ-action on G factors through H ⋊ Γ, and 0 otherwise. (2) For G ∈ 𝒩 with pairwise non-isomorphic compatible irreducible F ⋊ Γ-structures G_1, …, G_k, Σ_i |Sur_{F⋊Γ}(R, G_i)|/|Aut_{F⋊Γ}(G_i)| equals the same double sum over 𝓔_𝒞(G, H). (Corollary 4.8) Hence for G ∈ 𝒜_H, (h_{H⋊Γ}(G)^{m} − 1)/(h_{H⋊Γ}(G) − 1) = Σ_{(E,π)∈𝓔_𝒞(G,H)} Σ_D ν(D, E)(|Y(D)|/|Y(H)|)^n/|Aut_{Γ,H}(E, π)| with m = m(𝒞, n, ϖ, G), and for G ∈ 𝒩, m(𝒞, n, ϖ, G) equals that sum. (Remark 4.9) The multiplicities depend only on (𝒞, n, H, G).
hypotheses: (SZ_Γ); 𝒞 finite; H admissible of level 𝒞.
proofSteps: |Sur_{F⋊Γ}(R, G)| is |Aut_{F⋊Γ}(G)| times the number of F ⋊ Γ-subgroups M of R with R/M ≅ G; for abelian R/M the action factors through H ⋊ Γ.

Sorting these M by the isomorphism class of the H-extension F/M → H, and using that every surjection of H-extensions from (𝓕_n)^𝒞 onto such an extension factors through F (Liu–Wood Proposition 8.7), the count is Σ_{(E,π)} |Sur_{Γ,H}((𝓕_n)^𝒞 → H, π)|/|Aut_{Γ,H}(E, π)|; then apply RG.3/counting-extension-maps.
Non-abelian case: group together the H-extensions whose kernels have the same Γ-structure.
Corollary 4.8: write R = ∏ G_i^{m_i} and use RG.3/products-of-irreducible-operator-groups (d): |Sur_{F⋊Γ}(R, G_i)| = h^{m_i} − 1 (abelian), m_i|Aut_{F⋊Γ}(G_i)| (non-abelian).
acceptance: Γ = Z/2, H = 1, 𝒞 = {Z/3 with σ = −1}: 𝓔_𝒞(Z/3, 1) has one element with |Aut_{Γ,1}| = 2, so (3^m − 1)/2 = (3^n − 1)/2 and m = n.

sources.locator: Proposition 4.7, Corollary 4.8 and Remark 4.9 with proofs, pp. 22–24
sources.match: Counts F ⋊ Γ-surjections from R onto an irreducible group through H-extensions of level 𝒞 and Lemma 4.6, compares with the count through multiplicities (Liu–Wood Theorem 7.1), and concludes that the multiplicities do not depend on ϖ.

nodes.title: The λ-invariants λ(𝒞, H, G)
nodes.statement: For a set 𝒞 of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups and a finite Γ-group H of level 𝒞: for G ∈ 𝒜_H, λ(𝒞, H, G) = (h_{H⋊Γ}(G) − 1) Σ_{(E,π)∈𝓔_𝒞(G,H)} |Aut_{Γ,H}(E, π)|⁻¹ (LWZB (4.10)); for G ∈ 𝒩, λ(𝒞, H, G) = Σ_{(E,π)∈𝓔_𝒞(G,H)} |Aut_{Γ,H}(E, π)|⁻¹ (4.11). For finite 𝒞 these are finite sums, non-zero for only finitely many G, and (4.17) λ(𝒞, H, G) = lim_n h_{H⋊Γ}(G)^{m(𝒞,n,H,G)}|Y(G)|^{−n} for G ∈ 𝒜_H and lim_n m(𝒞, n, H, G)|Y(G)|^{−n} for G ∈ 𝒩; λ > 0 iff 𝓔_𝒞(G, H) ≠ ∅, and then m → ∞. λ is nondecreasing in 𝒞; for an arbitrary set 𝒞 (Definition 5.14) λ(𝒞, H, G) = lim_i λ(𝒟_i, H, G) along any increasing exhaustion of 𝒞 by finite sets 𝒟_i, independent of the exhaustion. If H has Property E at level 𝒞 then λ(𝒞, H, Z/p) = 0 for Z/p with trivial action.
hypotheses: H of level 𝒞; for (4.17), (SZ_Γ) and H admissible.
proofSteps: Finiteness of support: an irreducible kernel of an extension of level 𝒞 is a power of a simple group in the subgroup-and-quotient closure of 𝒞 (Liu–Wood Corollary 6.12) with exponent at most |H ⋊ Γ| (Liu–Wood Lemma 6.1).

(4.17): in the formula of RG.3/multiplicities-via-extensions, D = E is the unique term with |Y(D)|/|Y(H)| = |Y(G)|, the others being smaller by admissibility (RG.0/admissible-gamma-groups (d)); divide by |Y(G)|^n and let n → ∞.
Monotonicity in 𝒞: 𝓔_𝒞(G, H) grows with 𝒞; for an exhaustion the limit is the sum over all extensions of level 𝒞, which does not depend on the exhaustion.
Property E: a non-split central extension of H by Z/p of level 𝒞 admits no surjection from H (by order), so under Property E there is none, and split ones are not admissible; hence 𝓔_𝒞(Z/p, H) = ∅.
acceptance: The λ's are the parameters of the limiting formulas (4.14), (5.13) and Theorem 5.15.

nodes.title: Limits of truncated products (Liu–Wood Lemma 8.11)
nodes.statement: Let a > 1, x_n → x in ℝ and y_n → ∞ (positive integers). Then f(x) = ∏_{i≥1}(1 − x a^{−i}) is continuous in x and lim_n ∏_{i=1}^{y_n}(1 − x_n a^{−i}) = ∏_{i≥1}(1 − x a^{−i}). Similarly (1 − c_n)^{m_n} → e^{−λ} when m_n c_n → λ and c_n → 0.
hypotheses: a > 1 real.
proofSteps: Only finitely many factors can have |x_n a^{−i}| ≥ 1/2 for n large (x_n is bounded); treat them directly.

For the rest take logarithms: |log(1 − t) + t| ≤ t² for |t| ≤ 1/2, so the tails are dominated by a summable sequence C a^{−i} uniformly in n; apply Tannery's theorem (Mathlib's tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence) and exponentiate.
The exponential limit is the standard (1 − c_n)^{m_n} = exp(m_n log(1 − c_n)).

sources.match: States the continuity of x ↦ ∏(1 − x a^{−i}) and the convergence of truncated products with converging parameters and diverging lengths, used to pass from (8.2) to (8.3).

nodes.title: The finite-level distribution and its limit (Theorem 4.12)
nodes.statement: Assume (SZ_Γ). Let 𝒞 be a finite set of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups, H a finite admissible Γ-group of level 𝒞, n ≥ 1 and u > −n. Then, with m = m(𝒞, n, H, G), Prob((X_{u,n})^𝒞 ≅ H) = |Sur_Γ(𝓕_n, H)| / (|Aut_Γ(H)| |Y(H)|^{n+u}) · ∏_{G∈𝒜_H} ∏_{k=0}^{m−1}(1 − h_{H⋊Γ}(G)^k |Y(G)|^{−n−u}) · ∏_{G∈𝒩}(1 − |Y(G)|^{−n−u})^m   (4.13). If H has Property E at level 𝒞, then as n → ∞ this tends to |Aut_Γ(H)|⁻¹|Y(H)|^{−u} ∏_{G∈𝒜_H} ∏_{i≥1}(1 − λ(𝒞, H, G) h_{H⋊Γ}(G)^{−i} |Y(G)|^{−u}) · ∏_{G∈𝒩} exp(−|Y(G)|^{−u} λ(𝒞, H, G))   (4.14), a product with finitely many factors different from 1. If H lacks Property E at level 𝒞, the probability (4.13) is 0 for every n. (The printed (4.14) carries no Property E hypothesis and is false in that case: source issue E6 here.)
hypotheses: (SZ_Γ); 𝒞 finite of |Γ|′-groups; H finite admissible of level 𝒞; n ≥ 1, u > −n.
proofSteps: (4.15): the probability is the sum over closed normal Γ-subgroups N of (𝓕_n)^𝒞 with quotient ≅ H of Prob([Y(r_1, …, r_{n+u})] = N), r_j uniform (RG.2/random-gamma-groups).
(4.16): Prob(Y(r_j) ∈ N^d for all j) = |Y(H)|^{−n−u}, by RG.0/y-map and RG.0/sections-and-y.

Conditionally on that event, [Y(r)] = N iff the images of the Y(r_j) generate R in the fundamental sequence (the reference to (7.1) in the printed proof is to (4.1), source issue E12 here), and Y(r) mod M has the law of Y(r′) for uniform r′ ∈ R; apply RG.3/y-generation-probability and Remark 4.9.
The number of N is |Sur_Γ(𝓕_n, H)|/|Aut_Γ(H)| (RG.1/free-admissible-universal-property (c)); this gives (4.13).
Limits: finitely many G have m ≠ 0 (RG.3/fundamental-exact-sequence); by (4.17) of RG.3/lambda-invariants and RG.3/tail-product-limit each factor converges; |Sur_Γ(𝓕_n, H)||Y(H)|^{−n} → 1 (4.18).

Property E: then λ(𝒞, H, G) ≠ 0 forces |Y(G)| ≥ 2 (trivial-action Z/p has λ = 0), which is what the limit of the factor with h^m = 1 + λ·|Y(G)|^n requires. Without Property E some trivial-action Z/p occurs with m ≥ 1 for every n, its k = 0 factor is 1 − 1 = 0, and the probability vanishes, as RG.1/property-e-criterion also shows.
acceptance: Γ = Z/2, H = 1, 𝒞 = {Z/3 with σ = −1}: (4.13) = ∏_{k<n}(1 − 3^{k−n−u}) and (4.14) = ∏_{i>u}(1 − 3^{−i}), the Cohen–Lenstra probability of a trivial 3-part.

nodes.title: Chief factor pairs of finite groups (Liu–Wood §6)
nodes.statement: A chief series of a finite group G is a chain 1 = G_0 ◁ G_1 ◁ ⋯ ◁ G_r = G of normal subgroups of G with each G_{i+1}/G_i a minimal normal subgroup of G/G_i. For a minimal normal subgroup M of G, ρ_M : G → Aut(M) is conjugation. A chief factor pair is a pair (M, A) of finite groups with M an irreducible A-group and A acting faithfully (so A ≤ Aut(M)); (M, A) ≅ (M′, A′) if some isomorphism α : M → M′ carries A onto A′ under α_* : Aut(M) → Aut(M′). CF(G) is the set of isomorphism classes of the pairs (G_{i+1}/G_i, ρ_{G_{i+1}/G_i}(G/G_i)) of a chief series; it does not depend on the series (Liu–Wood Lemma 6.3, a Jordan–Hölder theorem for chief factor pairs). For a set T of finite groups, CF(T) = ∪_{G∈T} CF(G). Properties: CF(G × J) = CF(G) ∪ CF(J); CF(G/N) ⊆ CF(G); if T is closed under subgroups and quotients then CF(T̄) = CF(T) for its closure T̄ under products, subgroups and quotients (Lemma 6.11); a simple group in T̄ lies in the subgroup-and-quotient closure of T (Corollary 6.12); for finite T, CF(T̄) is finite and, if every member of T has order ≤ ℓ, A/Inn(M) has order ≤ ℓ − 1 for every (M, A) ∈ CF(T̄) (Corollary 6.13).
hypotheses: G finite; chief factors are characteristically simple, so each is T^k for a simple group T.
proofSteps: Independence of the series: induction on |G|; if G_1 ≠ I_1 compare both series through G_1 × I_1, whose two orders of quotients give isomorphic chief factor pairs (Liu–Wood Lemma 6.3).
Products and quotients: concatenate chief series of G × 1 and 1 × J; refine a series through N for G/N.

Subgroups (Lemma 6.11): a chief series of J ≤ G passes through the G_i ∩ J, and the pairs between 1 and G_1 ∩ J arise from a subgroup J′ of a group G′ ∈ T realizing (G_1, ρ(G)); by induction CF(J) ⊆ CF(T).
Corollary 6.12: (T, Inn T) ∈ CF(T̄) for simple T ∈ T̄. Corollary 6.13: if (M, A) ∈ CF(G) with |G| ≤ ℓ then |M||A/Inn M| ≤ ℓ (abelian M) or |A| ≤ ℓ (non-abelian M), so |A/Inn M| ≤ ℓ/2.
acceptance: Mathlib has composition series of lattices (CompositionSeries.jordan_holder) but no chief series of groups or minimal normal subgroups; these are new here.

nodes.title: Γ-chief factor pairs (Definition 5.1, Lemma 5.2, Corollary 5.3)
nodes.statement: For a finite |Γ|′-Γ-group G, CF_Γ(G) is the set of (M, A) ∈ CF(G ⋊ Γ) with gcd(|M|, |Γ|) = 1 — the chief factor pairs of G ⋊ Γ coming from the normal subgroup G — and CF_Γ(𝒞) = ∪_{G∈𝒞} CF_Γ(G) for a set 𝒞 of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups. (Lemma 5.2) If 𝒞 is closed under Γ-subgroups and Γ-quotients then CF_Γ(𝒞̄) = CF_Γ(𝒞). (Corollary 5.3) If every member of 𝒞 has order at most ℓ, then for each (M, A) ∈ CF_Γ(𝒞̄) the largest divisor of |A/Inn(M)| prime to |Γ| is less than ℓ, and CF_Γ(𝒞̄) is finite.
hypotheses: (SZ_Γ), used in Lemma 5.2 to conjugate the images of Γ.
proofSteps: Γ-quotients and finite products create no new pairs, as for CF.

Γ-subgroups J ≤ G ∈ 𝒞: take a chief series of G ⋊ Γ through G and the induced series of J ⋊ Γ through the G_i ∩ J; the pairs between 1 and G_1 ∩ J are realized by a Γ′-subgroup of some G′ ∈ 𝒞, where Γ′ is a conjugate of Γ obtained from Schur–Zassenhaus conjugacy inside ρ^{−1}(α_*(A)); twisting the Γ-action on G′ by that conjugation keeps it in 𝒞 (LWZB Lemma 5.2).
Corollary 5.3: follow Liu–Wood Corollary 6.13 in G ⋊ Γ, discarding the factor of |Γ|.

nodes.title: Multiplicity bounds at level ℓ (Lemma 5.4)
nodes.statement: Assume (SZ_Γ). Let H be a finite Γ-group of level 𝒞_ℓ and H̃ = H^{𝒞_{ℓ−1}}. If M is a product of isomorphic abelian simple groups, the number of G ∈ 𝒜_H with G ≅ M as groups and m(𝒞_ℓ, n, H, G) ≠ 0 for some n is at most Σ_{(M,A)∈CF_Γ(𝒞_ℓ)} |Sur(H̃ ⋊ Γ, A)|. If M is a product of isomorphic non-abelian simple groups, the number of isomorphism classes of level-𝒞_ℓ H-extensions (E, π) with ker π ≅ M an irreducible E ⋊ Γ-group is at most Σ_{(M,A)∈CF_Γ(𝒞_ℓ)} |Sur(H̃ ⋊ Γ, A/Inn(M))|. (The printed 'irred. E-group' is read as irreducible E ⋊ Γ-group, source issue E8 here.)
hypotheses: (SZ_Γ); 𝒞_ℓ the |Γ|′-Γ-groups of order ≤ ℓ.
proofSteps: An abelian factor G of R gives (G, ρ_G(F ⋊ Γ)) ∈ CF_Γ(𝒞_ℓ) and a surjection H ⋊ Γ → ρ_G(F ⋊ Γ); the map (G, φ) ↦ ((M, A), ρ) is injective (an equal image gives an H ⋊ Γ-isomorphism).
A non-abelian extension (E, π) maps to ((ker π, ρ(E ⋊ Γ)), the induced H ⋊ Γ → A/Inn(M)); E ⋊ Γ is the fibre product of H ⋊ Γ → A/Inn(M) ← A, so the map is injective.
By RG.4/gamma-chief-factor-pairs (Corollary 5.3) every surjection H ⋊ Γ → A/Inn(M) factors through H̃ ⋊ Γ.
acceptance: The bounds depend only on (ℓ, H̃), not on H or n — the input to Corollary 5.9.

nodes.title: A uniform lower bound for the generation factors (Corollary 5.9)
nodes.statement: Assume (SZ_Γ). For a finite Γ-group H of level 𝒞_ℓ let P_{u,n}(U_{𝒞_ℓ,H}) = ∏_{G∈𝒜_H} ∏_{k<m}(1 − h_{H⋊Γ}(G)^k |Y(G)|^{−n−u}) ∏_{G∈𝒩}(1 − |Y(G)|^{−n−u})^m (m = m(𝒞_ℓ, n, H, G)), the product in (4.13) without its prefactor. For ℓ > 1, integers u, and a finite Γ-group H̃ of level 𝒞_{ℓ−1}, there is c(u, ℓ, H̃) > 0 such that for all n ≥ 1 with u > −n and every H of level 𝒞_ℓ with H^{𝒞_{ℓ−1}} ≅ H̃, either P_{u,n}(U_{𝒞_ℓ,H}) = 0 or P_{u,n}(U_{𝒞_ℓ,H}) ≥ c(u, ℓ, H̃).
hypotheses: (SZ_Γ).
proofSteps: Abelian factors: by Remark 4.4 each non-zero abelian product is a product of distinct factors 1 − p^{−i}, hence ≥ ∏_{k≥1}(1 − 2^{−k}); Lemma 5.4 bounds the number of G involved by a constant depending only on (ℓ, H̃) (Liu–Wood Lemma 9.5).

Non-abelian factors: bound Σ_G m(𝒞_ℓ, n, H, G)|Y(G)|^{−n} using Corollary 4.8, Lemma 4.6, Corollary 3.8 and Lemma 5.4, uniformly in n; then (1 − |Y(G)|^{−n−u})^m ≥ exp(−C·m|Y(G)|^{−n−u}) gives a positive bound (Liu–Wood Lemmas 9.5–9.6).
acceptance: For abelian 𝒞 the bound is the Cohen–Lenstra constant ∏_{i≥1}(1 − p^{−i}) raised to the number of primes involved.

nodes.title: Interchanging limits and sums over the level tower (Lemma 5.10)
nodes.statement: Let f_n(H, ℓ) ≥ 0 be defined for n ≥ n_0, ℓ ≥ 1 and finite Γ-groups H of level 𝒞_ℓ, with: (1) f_n(H, ℓ) = g_n(H, ℓ) P_{u,n}(U_{𝒞_ℓ,H}); (2) g_n(H, ℓ) → g(H, ℓ) and g_n(H, ℓ) ≤ g(H, ℓ) for all n; (3) Σ_{H : H^{𝒞_{ℓ−1}} ≅ H̃} f_n(H, ℓ) = f_n(H̃, ℓ − 1); (4) if f_n(H, ℓ) > 0 then f_{n′}(H, ℓ) > 0 for all n′ ≥ n (monotone positivity, absent from the printed statement and needed by its proof: source issue E7 here). Then lim_n f_n(H, ℓ) exists for all (H, ℓ) and Σ_{H of level 𝒞_ℓ} lim_n f_n(H, ℓ) = lim_n f_n(1, 1). For u < 0 take n_0 = 1 − u.
hypotheses: (SZ_Γ) through Corollary 5.9; the four hypotheses above.
proofSteps: Existence of lim_n f_n: by (1), (2) and the convergence of P_{u,n} in the proof of Theorem 4.12.
Induction on ℓ; the case ℓ = 1 is the trivial group alone. By (3) it suffices to interchange limit and sum over the H above a fixed H̃.

For each H with f_n(H, ℓ) > 0 for some n, (4) and Corollary 5.9 give f_n(H, ℓ) ≥ ½c(u, ℓ, H̃)g(H, ℓ) for all large n; so Σ_H g(H, ℓ) ≤ (2/c) lim_n f_n(H̃, ℓ − 1) < ∞ and the f_n(H, ℓ) are dominated by the summable g(H, ℓ).
Dominated convergence for sums (Mathlib's tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence) gives the interchange.
acceptance: Both applications satisfy (4): killing the generator x_{n+1} identifies 𝓕_{n+1}/[Y(S ∪ {y})] with 𝓕_n/[Y(S)] when Y(y) = Y(x_{n+1}), so an event of positive probability at n stays positive at n + 1.

nodes.title: No escape of mass: countable additivity of μ_u (Theorem 5.12)
nodes.statement: Assume (SZ_Γ). For every integer u, the set function μ_u(A) = lim_n μ_{u,n}(A) on the algebra 𝒜 generated by the basic opens exists and is countably additive on 𝒜, with μ_u(𝒫) = 1. In particular Σ_{H of level 𝒞_ℓ} μ_u(U_{𝒞_ℓ,H}) = 1 for every ℓ. (The printed theorem assumes u ≥ 0; its proof never uses it, and Theorems 5.15, 6.2 and 7.4–7.5 need every u: source issue E9 here.)
hypotheses: (SZ_Γ); u any integer, with X_{u,n} defined for n > −u.
proofSteps: Existence of the limit on basic opens is RG.3/finite-level-distribution (limit 0 when Property E fails); finite additivity passes to the limit, so μ_u is a finitely additive content on 𝒜 with μ_u(𝒫) = 1.

Tightness: apply RG.4/limit-interchange with f_n(H, ℓ) = μ_{u,n}(U_{𝒞_ℓ,H}) and g_n(H) = |Sur_Γ(𝓕_n, H)|/(|Aut_Γ(H)||Y(H)|^{n+u}), whose limit is |Aut_Γ(H)|⁻¹|Y(H)|^{−u} for admissible H by (4.18) (and 0 otherwise); this gives Σ_H μ_u(U_{𝒞_ℓ,H}) = μ_u(U_{𝒞_1,1}) = 1.

Countable additivity on 𝒜 follows from tightness at every level, as in Liu–Wood Corollary 9.7 and Theorem 9.1: a countable disjoint union in 𝒜 of level-ℓ basic opens has measure the sum, and every countable disjoint decomposition in 𝒜 refines to one of this form.
acceptance: μ_u(𝒫) = 1 for every u; for Γ = Z/2 and 𝒞 the abelian 3-Γ-groups, the masses of the V_{𝒞,H} sum to 1 (the Cohen–Lenstra mass formula, ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/cohen-lenstra-mass-formula, for u ≥ 0).

nodes.statement: Assume (SZ_Γ). For each integer u, μ_u is the unique Borel probability measure on 𝒫 extending the countably additive content μ_u on 𝒜 (Carathéodory); μ_Γ = μ_1. The basic opens and the algebra 𝒜 generate the Borel σ-algebra, so μ_u is determined by its values on basic opens, and μ_u(V_{𝒞,H}) = lim_i μ_u(U_{𝒟_i,H}) for an exhaustion of an arbitrary 𝒞 by finite sets.

proofSteps: 𝒜 is a ring of sets (in particular a set semiring) and μ_u is σ-additive, hence σ-subadditive, on it (RG.4/countable-additivity); Mathlib's AddContent.measure gives a measure on the σ-algebra generated by 𝒜, which is the Borel σ-algebra (RG.2/space-of-admissible-gamma-groups), agreeing with μ_u on 𝒜 (AddContent.measure_eq).

Continuity from above gives μ_u(V_{𝒞,H}) as the decreasing limit.

nodes.title: Convergence of the random Γ-groups (Theorem 1.2)
nodes.statement: Assume (SZ_Γ). For every finite group Γ, the laws μ_{1,n} of X_{Γ,n} = 𝓕_n/[Y(S)] (|S| = n + 1) converge weakly to the probability measure μ_Γ on 𝒫 as n → ∞; more generally μ_{u,n} → μ_u for every integer u. Explicitly (5.13), for a finite set 𝒞 of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups and a finite admissible Γ-group H of level 𝒞 with Property E at level 𝒞, μ_Γ(U_{𝒞,H}) = |Aut_Γ(H)|⁻¹ [H : H^Γ]⁻¹ ∏_{G∈𝒜_H} ∏_{i≥1}(1 − λ(𝒞, H, G) h_{H⋊Γ}(G)^{−i} [G : G^Γ]⁻¹) ∏_{G∈𝒩} exp(−λ(𝒞, H, G)/[G : G^Γ]); if H is not admissible or lacks Property E at level 𝒞, μ_Γ(U_{𝒞,H}) = 0. (The printed (5.13) has no Property E hypothesis: source issue E6 here.)
hypotheses: (SZ_Γ).
proofSteps: Every open set U ⊆ 𝒫 is a countable disjoint union of basic opens U_j (RG.2/space-of-admissible-gamma-groups); μ_Γ(U) = Σ_j lim_n μ_{1,n}(U_j) ≤ liminf_n Σ_j μ_{1,n}(U_j) = liminf_n μ_{1,n}(U) by Fatou's lemma for sums (the printed proof writes lim for liminf, source issue E10 here).
Weak convergence follows from the open-set criterion of the Portmanteau theorem (Mathlib's MeasureTheory.tendsto_of_forall_isOpen_le_liminf; the filter atTop is countably generated).
(5.13) is (4.14) with u = 1 and |Y(G)| = [G : G^Γ] (RG.0/y-map); the vanishing case is the last clause of RG.3/finite-level-distribution.
acceptance: Γ = Z/2, 𝒞 = {Z/3 with σ = −1}, H = Z/3: here λ = 1/3 and μ_Γ(U_{𝒞,H}) = (1/6)∏_{i≥3}(1 − 3^{−i}) = (3/16)∏_{i≥2}(1 − 3^{−i}), the real-quadratic (u = 1) Cohen–Lenstra probability that the 3-rank is exactly 1.
Γ = Z/2, H = F_3² with σ = −1 at the level of 3-class ≤ 2: μ_Γ(U_{𝒞,H}) = 0.

sources.match: States weak convergence of the laws of X_{Γ,n} to μ_Γ and proves it from countable additivity, the decomposition of open sets into basic opens and Fatou's lemma, giving the explicit value (5.13) on basic opens.

nodes.title: μ_u on V_{𝒞,H} for arbitrary 𝒞 (Definition 5.14, Theorem 5.15)
nodes.statement: Assume (SZ_Γ). Let 𝒞 be an arbitrary set of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups, H a finite admissible Γ-group of level 𝒞 with Property E at level 𝒞, and u an integer. With m and λ extended to 𝒞 by exhaustion (Definition 5.14), μ_u(V_{𝒞,H}) = |Aut_Γ(H)|⁻¹|Y(H)|^{−u} ∏_{G∈𝒜_H} ∏_{i≥1}(1 − λ(𝒞, H, G) h_{H⋊Γ}(G)^{−i}|Y(G)|^{−u}) ∏_{G∈𝒩} exp(−|Y(G)|^{−u} λ(𝒞, H, G)). If H lacks Property E at level 𝒞, μ_u(V_{𝒞,H}) = 0. (The printed theorem has no Property E hypothesis and is false for such H: source issue E6 here.)
hypotheses: (SZ_Γ); H finite admissible of level 𝒞.
proofSteps: V_{𝒞,H} = ⋂_i U_{𝒟_i,H} for an exhaustion 𝒟_1 ⊆ 𝒟_2 ⊆ ⋯ with H of level 𝒟_i, so μ_u(V_{𝒞,H}) = lim_i μ_u(U_{𝒟_i,H}) by continuity from above (RG.4/limit-measure, which needs Theorem 5.12 for this u).

Each μ_u(U_{𝒟_i,H}) is the product (4.14); its factors are non-increasing in i and λ(𝒟_i, H, G) increases to λ(𝒞, H, G) (RG.3/lambda-invariants), so the limit is the product with the limiting λ's (Liu–Wood Lemma 11.3 with Lemma 8.11).

Level-𝒟_i groups are of level 𝒞, so Property E at level 𝒞 gives Property E at level 𝒟_i once H is of level 𝒟_i (RG.1/property-e-at-level (a)), and the formula follows. If H lacks Property E at level 𝒞, the obstructing extension G̃ → G is finite, hence of level 𝒟_i for large i; then μ_u(U_{𝒟_i,H}) = 0 and V_{𝒞,H} ⊆ U_{𝒟_i,H}, because X^𝒞 ≅ H gives X^{𝒟_i} ≅ H^{𝒟_i} = H.
acceptance: Γ = Z/2, p = 3, 𝒞 all finite 3-Γ-groups, H = F_3² with σ = −1: μ_u(V_{𝒞,H}) = 0 (the printed formula gives 2.70·10^{−3} at u = 0, while Theorem 7.4 gives 0).
For abelian 𝒞 this is the formula of §7.1 (RG.5/abelian-specialization).

nodes.title: Moments at finite n (Lemma 6.1)
nodes.statement: Assume (SZ_Γ). For a finite admissible Γ-group A and integers n ≥ 1, u > −n: E|Sur_Γ(X_{u,n}, A)| = |Sur_Γ(𝓕_n, A)| · |Y(A)|^{−n−u}, and this tends to [A : A^Γ]^{−u} as n → ∞.
hypotheses: (SZ_Γ); A finite admissible (in particular of order prime to |Γ|).
proofSteps: A Γ-surjection X_{u,n} → A is a Γ-surjection φ : 𝓕_n → A whose kernel contains the coordinates of every Y(s_j); so E|Sur_Γ(X_{u,n}, A)| = Σ_φ Prob(Y(s_j) ∈ (ker φ)^d for all j).
Each probability is |Y(A)|^{−n−u} by (4.16) (RG.0/y-map with RG.0/sections-and-y).
|Sur_Γ(𝓕_n, A)||Y(A)|^{−n} → 1 (RG.1/free-admissible-universal-property (b)) and |Y(A)| = [A : A^Γ].

sources.match: Computes the expected number of Γ-surjections from X_{u,n} to a finite admissible A as |Sur_Γ(𝓕_n, A)||Y(A)|^{−n−u} and its limit [A : A^Γ]^{−u}.

nodes.title: The moments of μ_u (Theorem 6.2)
nodes.statement: Assume (SZ_Γ). For every integer u and every finite admissible Γ-group A, X ↦ |Sur_Γ(X, A)| is a locally constant function on 𝒫 and ∫ |Sur_Γ(X, A)| dμ_u(X) = [A : A^Γ]^{−u}. In particular the μ_Γ-moment is [A : A^Γ]^{−1}, and for abelian A with A^Γ = 1 it is |A|^{−1}.
hypotheses: (SZ_Γ); A finite admissible; u any integer (this uses Theorem 5.12 for all u).
proofSteps: For ℓ ≥ |A|, |Sur_Γ(X, A)| = |Sur_Γ(X^{𝒞_ℓ}, A)|, so the function is constant on each U_{𝒞_ℓ,H} and the integral is Σ_H |Sur_Γ(H, A)| μ_u(U_{𝒞_ℓ,H}).

Apply RG.4/limit-interchange to f_n(H, ℓ) = E(|Sur_Γ(X_{u,n}, A)| · 1[X_{u,n}^{𝒞_ℓ} ≅ H]); conditioning on Y(S̄) as in the proof of LWZB Theorem 6.2 gives f_n = g_n P_{u,n}(U_{𝒞_ℓ,H}) with g_n = |Y(A^{𝒞_ℓ})|^{n+u}|Sur_Γ(ρ, π_A)||Sur_Γ((𝓕_n)^{𝒞_ℓ}, H)||Sur_Γ(H, A^{𝒞_ℓ})| / (|Y(A)|^{n+u}|Y(H)|^{n+u}|Aut_Γ(H)|), bounded by its limit (RG.3/counting-extension-maps and RG.1/free-admissible-universal-property).

Monotone positivity holds as in RG.4/limit-interchange; the sum over H of lim_n f_n is lim_n E|Sur_Γ(X_{u,n}, A)| = [A : A^Γ]^{−u} (RG.5/finite-n-moments), and for ℓ ≥ |A| the left side is Σ_H |Sur_Γ(H, A)|μ_u(U_{𝒞_ℓ,H}).
acceptance: Γ = Z/2, A = Z/3 with σ = −1: the μ_1-moment is 1/3 and the μ_0-moment is 1, i.e. averages 4/3 and 2 of |Cl[3]| for real and imaginary quadratic fields, the Davenport–Heilbronn values.
Γ = Z/4 acting on the Heisenberg group of order 27 through a fixed-point-free action of order 4 on its abelianization (trivially on the centre): A^Γ is the centre, so the moment is 1/9 (LWZB §1.5).
Γ = (Z/2)² acting faithfully and admissibly on the Heisenberg group of order 27: A^Γ = 1 and the moment is 1/27 (LWZB §1.5).

nodes.title: Finite-index sublattices over Z_p[Γ] for p ∤ |Γ|
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime not dividing |Γ| and L = (Z_p[Γ]/(Σ_{g∈Γ} g))^n. Every Γ-stable Z_p-submodule N ⊆ L of finite index is isomorphic to L as a Z_p[Γ]-module. More generally, two Z_p[Γ]-lattices (finitely generated, Z_p-free) M ⊆ M′ with M′/M finite are isomorphic.
proofSteps: Lattices are projective Z_p[Γ]-modules: a Z_p-linear splitting of Z_p[Γ] ⊗ M → M, averaged over Γ (|Γ| is a unit), is Z_p[Γ]-linear (Mathlib's Module.Projective.of_split).

Reductions agree in the Grothendieck group: for T = M′/M finite, the snake lemma for multiplication by p on 0 → M → M′ → T → 0 gives an exact sequence 0 → T[p] → M/pM → M′/pM′ → T/pT → 0, and T[p], T/pT have the same composition factors (from 0 → T[p] → T → T → T/pT → 0).
F_p[Γ] is semisimple (Maschke, Mathlib's MonoidAlgebra.Submodule.exists_isCompl), so M/pM ≅ M′/pM′.

Lift an isomorphism M/pM → M′/pM′ to φ : M → M′ by projectivity; φ is onto by Nakayama (Mathlib's Submodule.le_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot, with p in the Jacobson radical) and injective because M and M′ are free of the same Z_p-rank.
acceptance: For Γ = Z/2, p = 3, n = 1: L = Z_3 with σ = −1 and every non-zero Γ-submodule 3^kZ_3 is isomorphic to L.
The hypothesis p ∤ |Γ| is needed: for Γ = Z/2, p = 2, the sublattice of Z_2[Γ] spanned by 1 + σ and 2 has finite index but its reduction mod 2 is the trivial module twice, not F_2[Γ].

sources.match: Uses that a finite-index closed Γ-submodule N_p of the pro-p abelian quotient of 𝓕_n is isomorphic to it, because Z_p[Γ] is hereditary and N_p ⊗ Q_p ≅ (𝓕_n)^𝒞_p ⊗ Q_p (citing Serre, Linear Representations, §16, Theorem 34, Corollary 2); the module is printed as Z_p[Γ]^n instead of (Z_p[Γ]/(Σg))^n (source issue E13 here).

nodes.title: The abelianization: the Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet distribution (§7.1)
nodes.statement: Assume (SZ_Γ). Let 𝒞 be the set of all finite abelian |Γ|′-Γ-groups (or those whose orders involve only a fixed set of primes not dividing |Γ|), and H a finite abelian |Γ|′-Γ-group with H^Γ = 1. Then: (a) in every fundamental sequence 1 → R → F → H → 1 at level 𝒞 the H-action on R is trivial and F^Γ = R^Γ = H^Γ = 1, so m(𝒞, n, H, G) = 0 unless G ∈ 𝒜_H has trivial H-action; (b) for G with trivial H-action and G^Γ = 1, m(𝒞, n, H, G) = n·m_G (m_G maximal with G^{m_G} cyclic as a Γ-module, h_Γ(G)^{m_G} = |G|) and λ(𝒞, H, G) = 1; (c) μ_u(V_{𝒞,H}) = |Aut_Γ(H)|^{−1} |H|^{−u} ∏_{p∤|Γ|} ∏_{G} ∏_{i≥1}(1 − h_Γ(G)^{−i}|G|^{−u}), the middle product over the non-trivial irreducible F_p[Γ]-modules G (restricted to the chosen primes). For u = 1 this is the Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet distribution of the prime-to-|Γ| class groups of totally real Γ-fields; for Γ = Z/2 and u = 0, 1 its p-parts are the Cohen–Lenstra measures μ_{p,u}.
hypotheses: (SZ_Γ) (abelian H needs it only through the general machinery); H^Γ = 1.
proofSteps: (a) In an abelian level the kernel R is abelian with trivial F-conjugation, hence trivial H-action; (𝓕_n^ab)^Γ = 0 (RG.1/free-admissible-universal-property (d)) gives F^Γ = 1.

(b) For a finite-index closed Γ-subgroup N of (𝓕_n)^𝒞, N ≅ (𝓕_n)^𝒞 one prime at a time (RG.5/coprime-lattice-lemma), so the maximal quotient of N that is a product of copies of G has G^{n m_G}, giving m = n·m_G; by (4.17) λ = lim h^{n m_G}|G|^{−n} = 1 (Remark 4.4 with |Y(G)| = |G| because G^Γ = 1).
(c) Insert (b) into RG.4/arbitrary-level-values; |Y(H)| = |H| because H^Γ = 1; the trivial F_p[Γ]-module has m = 0 and λ = 0.

For Γ = Z/2 the only non-trivial irreducible F_p[Γ]-module is F_p with σ = −1, h_Γ = p, so the p-part is |Aut H|^{−1}|H|^{−u}∏_{i>u}(1 − p^{−i}) = μ_{p,u}(H) (ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/cohen-lenstra-measure). The agreement with Cohen–Martinet's formulation for general Γ is Wang–Wood, Proposition 6.5.
acceptance: For abelian H with H^Γ = 1 the moment |H|^{−1} of RG.5/moments equals the predicted Cohen–Martinet moment ∏_v |H^{σ_v}|^{−1} of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/cohen-martinet-predicted-surjection-moment for totally real fields (every σ_v = 1).

sources.match: Shows that for abelian levels the multiplicities are n·m_G and λ = 1, and that μ_u restricted to finite abelian |Γ|′-Γ-groups with trivial invariants is |Aut_Γ(H)|^{−1}|H|^{−u} times a product over non-trivial irreducible F_p[Γ]-modules, the Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet distribution for u = 1.

nodes.title: The p-covering group, p-multiplicator and nucleus
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime and H a finite p-group with generator rank d = d(H) = dim_{F_p} H/Φ(H). For n ≥ d and a surjection ϖ : F → H from a free pro-p group of rank n with kernel N, put N* = N^p[N, F], F′ = F/N* and R′ = N/N* (LWZB (7.1)); R′ is elementary abelian and central in F′, and F′ is the largest quotient of F mapping onto H with kernel elementary abelian with trivial F′-action. For n = d, F′ is the p-covering group of H and R′ its p-multiplicator; r(H) = dim_{F_p} R′ = dim H²(H, F_p) is the relation rank, and for n ≥ d, dim R′ = r(H) + n − d. The lower p-central series is P_0(P) = P, P_{i+1}(P) = [P_i(P), P]·P_i(P)^p, Q_i(P) = P/P_i(P), and the p-class cl_p(H) is the least c with P_c(H) = 1. If cl_p(H) = c, the nucleus of H is P_c(F′) ≤ R′ and ν(H) = dim_{F_p} P_c(F′) is the nuclear rank. When a group Γ of order prime to p acts on H and ϖ is Γ-equivariant, N, N*, F′, R′ and P_c(F′) are Γ-stable and the constructions are Γ-equivariant; for 𝒞 the p-Γ-groups of p-class at most c, (𝓕_n)^𝒞 = Q_c((𝓕_n)_p).
hypotheses: H a finite p-group; for the Γ-structure, p ∤ |Γ|.
proofSteps: N* is characteristic in N and normal in F, so F′ and R′ are well defined; R′ is elementary abelian and central because N^p[N, F] ⊇ N^p[N, N].

Independence of the presentation: two surjections from free pro-p groups of rank d differ by an automorphism of F (Gaschütz lifting of generators, tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 3), so F′ is unique up to isomorphism over H.

dim R′ = r(H) + n − d: R′ is dual to H¹(N, F_p)^F, which the five-term sequence and H²(F, F_p) = 0 identify with H¹(F, F_p)/inflation ⊕ H²(H, F_p) of dimension (n − d) + r(H) (ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 5, the H² interpretation).

The lower p-central series and p-class are ProfiniteProPGroups' pLowerCentralSeries; Q_c((𝓕_n)_p) is of level 𝒞 and universal for maps to p-groups of p-class ≤ c, which is (𝓕_n)^𝒞 (RG.1/level-completion).
acceptance: For H = (Z/p)^d, r(H) = d(d + 1)/2, the sanity value in ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 5.

nodes.title: The pro-p specialization: Boston–Bush–Hajir (Lemma 7.2, Theorem 7.4)
nodes.statement: Let Γ = Z/2 = ⟨σ⟩, p an odd prime and u an integer. (Lemma 7.2) If H is an admissible p-Γ-group and ϖ : (𝓕_n)_p → H a Γ-surjection whose kernel is generated as a closed normal Γ-subgroup by the coordinates of Y(S) for a finite S, then for every finite set 𝒞 of p-Γ-groups with H of level 𝒞 the fundamental sequence is (F′)^𝒞 → H induced by (7.1), and for 𝒞 large enough it is (7.1). (Theorem 7.4) Let 𝒞 be the set of all finite p-Γ-groups and H a finite p-Γ-group. If H ≅ (𝓕_n)^𝒞/[Y(S)] for some n and some S with |S| = n + u, then μ_u(V_{𝒞,H}) = |Aut_Γ(H)|^{−1}|Y(H)|^{−u} ∏_{i ≥ 1+u+d(H)−r(H)} (1 − p^{−i}); otherwise μ_u(V_{𝒞,H}) = 0. For u = 0 and u = 1 these are the Boston–Bush–Hajir measures predicted for the p-class tower groups of imaginary and real quadratic fields.
hypotheses: (SZ_Γ) holds (Γ = Z/2 is solvable); p odd.
proofSteps: Lemma 7.2: by the Y-generation of the kernel, σ acts by −1 on every irreducible factor G of R; as G is an irreducible p-group-module it is Z/p with trivial H-action, so F′ → H factors through F; conversely F → H factors through the largest level-𝒞 quotient of F′.

Theorem 7.4: by RG.4/arbitrary-level-values only G = Z/p (trivial H-action, σ = −1) has λ ≠ 0, with |Y(G)| = h_{H⋊Γ}(G) = p; m(𝒞, n, H, G) = r(H) − d(H) + n (Liu–Wood Lemma 12.5 with RG.5/p-covering-group), so λ = p^{r(H)−d(H)} by (4.17).

Then ∏_{i≥1}(1 − p^{r−d}p^{−i}p^{−u}) = ∏_{j≥1+u+d−r}(1 − p^{−j}); the vanishing case is the support statement of RG.4/arbitrary-level-values (H without Property E, equivalently not of the stated form by RG.1/property-e-criterion).

Agreement with Boston–Bush–Hajir: for u = 0 Boston–Wood Lemma 4.8, for u = 1 Boston–Bush–Hajir (2021), Theorem 2.22, with equality of supports from Boston–Bush–Hajir (2017), Lemma 2.7, and (2021), Lemma 2.8.
acceptance: H = Z/3 (σ = −1), u = 1: d = r = 1 and μ_1(V_{𝒞,H}) = (1/6)∏_{i≥2}(1 − 3^{−i}) = μ_{3,1}(Z/3), consistent with RG.5/abelian-specialization because a cyclic 3-class group has trivial 3-class field tower beyond it.
H = 1: μ_u(V_{𝒞,1}) = ∏_{i≥1+u}(1 − p^{−i}), the Cohen–Lenstra probability of a trivial p-part.
H = F_3² with σ = −1 is not of the stated form (it lacks Property E), so μ_u(V_{𝒞,H}) = 0.

nodes.title: The p-class-c specialization (Theorem 7.5)
nodes.statement: Let Γ = Z/2, p odd, u an integer, c ≥ 1, and 𝒞 the set of finite p-Γ-groups of p-class at most c. For H of the form (𝓕_n)^𝒞/[Y(S)] with |S| = n + u: (1) if cl_p(H) < c then m(𝒞, n, H, G) = r(H) + n − d(H) and μ_u(V_{𝒞,H}) = |Aut_Γ(H)|^{−1}|Y(H)|^{−u} ∏_{i ≥ 1+u+d(H)−r(H)}(1 − p^{−i}); (2) if cl_p(H) = c then m(𝒞, n, H, G) = r(H) − ν(H) + n − d(H) and μ_u(V_{𝒞,H}) = |Aut_Γ(H)|^{−1}|Y(H)|^{−u} ∏_{i ≥ 1+u+d(H)+ν(H)−r(H)}(1 − p^{−i}). If H is not of this form, μ_u(V_{𝒞,H}) = 0. For u = 0, 1 these are the Boston–Bush–Hajir measures on p-class-c quotients.
hypotheses: Γ = Z/2; p odd; c ≥ 1.
proofSteps: (𝓕_n)^𝒞 = Q_c((𝓕_n)_p) (RG.5/p-covering-group).
If cl_p(H) < c, P_c(F′) = 1 because P_{c−1}(F′) lies in the elementary abelian central kernel; so F′ is of p-class ≤ c and the fundamental sequence is (7.1) (Remark 7.3).
If cl_p(H) = c, P_c((𝓕_n)_p) ≤ N and the fundamental sequence is F′/P_c(F′) → H with kernel R′/P_c(F′), of dimension r(H) − ν(H) + n − d(H).
Insert the multiplicities into RG.4/arbitrary-level-values as in Theorem 7.4.
acceptance: c = 1: the p-class-1 groups are the elementary abelian p-Γ-groups; for H = F_p^d (σ = −1), ν(H) = r(H) and μ_u(V_{𝒞,H}) = |GL_d(F_p)|^{−1}p^{−du}∏_{i≥1+u+d}(1 − p^{−i}), the Cohen–Lenstra probability that the p-rank is d.

nodes.title: The Liu–Wood–Zureick-Brown conjecture (Conjecture 1.3), as a proposition
nodes.statement: Let Q be Q, or F_q(t) with q prime to |Γ|, and Δ = 2|Γ| for Q = Q, Δ = q(q − 1)|Γ| for Q = F_q(t). A Γ-extension K/Q is a Galois extension with an identification Gal(K/Q) ≅ Γ; it is totally real when it is split completely above ∞. K^# is the maximal extension of K unramified everywhere, split completely above ∞, all of whose finite subextensions have degree prime to Δ; Gal(K^#/K) is an admissible Γ-group through a Schur–Zassenhaus section, well defined up to isomorphism (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.4/unramified-gamma-groups, under (SZ_Γ)). rDisc(K) is the norm of the radical of the discriminant ideal of K/Q, and E_Γ(D, Q) the finite set of isomorphism classes of totally real Γ-extensions with rDisc(K) = D. LWZBConjecture(Γ, Q) is the proposition: for every finite set 𝒞 of finite Γ-groups of order prime to Δ and every finite admissible Γ-group H of order prime to Δ, (i) Σ_{D≤B} #{K ∈ E_Γ(D, Q) : Gal(K^#/K)^𝒞 ≅ H^𝒞} / Σ_{D≤B} |E_Γ(D, Q)| → μ_Γ(U_{𝒞,H^𝒞}) as B → ∞, and (ii) Σ_{D≤B} Σ_{K∈E_Γ(D,Q)} |Sur_Γ(Gal(K^#/K), H)| / Σ_{D≤B} |E_Γ(D, Q)| → ∫|Sur_Γ(X, H)| dμ_Γ = [H : H^Γ]^{−1}. It is recorded as a proposition and never assumed.
hypotheses: (SZ_Γ) for the Γ-action on Gal(K^#/K) and for μ_Γ; q prime to |Γ| in the function-field case.
proofSteps: E_Γ(D, Q) is finite: the discriminant of K/Q is bounded in terms of D and |Γ|, and Hermite's theorem (Mathlib's NumberField.finite_of_discr_bdd) or its function-field analogue applies.
Gal(K^#/K)^𝒞 is finite for finite 𝒞 (RG.6/conjecture-consistency), so the counts in (i) are counts of finitely many conditions.
The right sides are μ_Γ of a basic open (RG.4/weak-convergence) and the moment of RG.5/moments; both statements are propositions about limits of explicit finite averages.
acceptance: The proposition is well formed for every finite Γ; it is consistent with the support of μ_Γ (RG.6/conjecture-consistency).

nodes.title: The Galois groups lie in the support of μ_Γ
nodes.statement: Assume (SZ_Γ). Let K/Q be a Γ-extension (Q = Q or F_q(t)) and 𝒞 a finite set of finite Γ-groups of order prime to Δ. (a) Gal(K^#/K)^𝒞 is a finite admissible Γ-group with Property E at level 𝒞, and the class of Gal(K^#/K) lies in 𝒫. (b) μ_Γ(U_{𝒞,H}) = 0 unless H is admissible with Property E at level 𝒞, so form (i) of the conjecture predicts positive frequency only for groups the Galois side allows. (c) Gal(K^#/K)^ab is the prime-to-Δ part of the class group (Cl(O_K) for Q = Q; the prime-to-q(q−1)|Γ| part of Cl(O_K), O_K the integral closure of F_q[t], for Q = F_q(t)); hence at abelian levels form (i) is the Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet prediction with u = 1 (RG.5/abelian-specialization).
hypotheses: (SZ_Γ); K a Γ-extension of Q or F_q(t).
proofSteps: (a) Admissibility is LWZB Proposition 2.2 and Property E for Δ′-Γ-groups is Theorem 2.5 (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.4/unramified-gamma-groups and IG.4/unramified-property-e); RG.1/property-e-at-level (b) passes Property E to the level-𝒞 completion.

Finiteness of Gal(K^#/K)^𝒞: K has finitely many unramified extensions of bounded degree (Hermite), so finitely many Γ-maps to the members of 𝒞, and the intersection of their kernels has finite index; this places the class in 𝒫.
(b) is the support clause of RG.4/weak-convergence.

(c) is class field theory: the maximal unramified abelian extension split completely at the infinite places is the Hilbert class field (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory Layer 12) or, over F_q(t), the extension with Galois group Cl(O_K) (FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.4); restrict to the prime-to-Δ part.
acceptance: For Γ = Z/2 and Q = Q, Gal(K^#/K)^ab is the odd part of the class group of the real quadratic field K, and its abelian level-3 predictions are the u = 1 Cohen–Lenstra probabilities.
For Γ = Z/2, p = 3 and H = F_3² with σ = −1 at 3-class ≤ 2, no real quadratic K has Gal(K^#/K)^𝒞 ≅ H, consistently with μ_Γ(U_{𝒞,H}) = 0.

nodes.title: Function-field moments agree with the moments of μ_Γ
nodes.statement: Assume (SZ_Γ). Let H be a finite admissible Γ-group and q range over prime powers with gcd(q, |Γ||H|) = 1 and gcd(q − 1, |H|) = 1. The function-field moment theorem ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/liu-wood-zureick-brown-function-field-moments gives lim_{b→∞} limsup_{q→∞} R_b(q) = lim_{b→∞} liminf_{q→∞} R_b(q) = [H : H^Γ]^{−1} for the averages R_b(q) of |Sur_Γ(Gal(K^#/K), H)| over E_Γ(q^n, F_q(t)), n ≤ b. By RG.5/moments this common value is ∫|Sur_Γ(X, H)| dμ_Γ(X). Hence form (ii) of the conjecture holds over F_q(t) in the iterated limit, q → ∞ first, for every such H; for abelian H with H^Γ = 1 this is the Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet moment |H|^{−1} of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/cohen-lenstra-martinet-moments-over-function-fields.
hypotheses: (SZ_Γ) (ST.5 states the moment theorem under the same hypothesis); the coprimality conditions on q.
proofSteps: Read the right side of the ST.5 theorem, [H : H^Γ]^{−1}.
Identify it with the μ_Γ-moment by RG.5/moments with u = 1.
The inner limit in q is read with lim sup and lim inf, because the existence of lim_{q→∞} R_b(q) is not proved (ST.5 records this).
acceptance: Γ = Z/2, H = Z/3 with σ = −1: the iterated function-field average of |Sur(Cl(O_K), Z/3)| is 1/3 = ∫|Sur_Γ(X, Z/3)|dμ_Γ.
The comparison is an identity of numbers; it asserts nothing about the number-field case of the conjecture.

nodes.title: p-class tower groups occur in the model (Lemma 3.17, Proposition 3.22)
nodes.statement: Assume (SZ_Γ). Let K/Q be a Γ-extension (Q = Q or F_q(t)) and p ∤ Δ a prime with μ_p ⊄ K. Let G_{K,p} be the maximal pro-p quotient of Gal(K^#/K) (the Galois group of the maximal unramified pro-p extension of K split completely above ∞) and G̃_{K,p} the Galois group of the maximal unramified pro-p extension of K. (Lemma 3.17) For the presentations ρ : F → G̃_{K,p} of §3.3 (F = (F_n)_p over Q, F = (F_{n+1})_p over F_q(t), the extra generator mapping to a decomposition group at an infinite place), N = ker ρ and N* = [N, F]N^p, there is an F_p[Γ]-surjection F_p[Γ]^{n+1} → N/N*. (Proposition 3.22) If n is so large that G_{K,p} = [Y({h_1, …, h_n})] for some h_i ∈ G_{K,p}, then G_{K,p} ≅ (𝓕_n)_p/[Y(S)] for a subset S ⊆ (𝓕_n)_p with |S| = n + 1. So every p-class tower group of a totally real Γ-field is of the shape of the random groups X_{1,n}.
hypotheses: (SZ_Γ); p ∤ Δ; μ_p ⊄ K.
proofSteps: G_{K,p} is finitely presented and admissible (Koch, Chapter 11; IG.4/unramified-gamma-groups), so the h_i exist for n large.

Lemma 3.17: by the five-term sequence (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology Layer 5) and H²(F, F_p) = 0 for free pro-p F (ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 5), (N/N*)^∨ = H¹(N, F_p)^F is an extension of H²(G̃_{K,p}, F_p) by the image of restriction, which is (N/(N ∩ Φ(F)))^∨; F_p[Γ] is semisimple, so it splits.

H²(G̃_{K,p}, F_p) embeds into (V/K^{×p})^∨ (Koch, Theorem 11.3; requested from ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.3), and V/K^{×p} is an extension of Cl(O_K)[p] by O_K^×/O_K^{×p}, which embeds in F_p[Γ]/(Σg) (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, Corollary 8.7.3; same request). Counting F_p[Γ]-ranks gives the surjection from F_p[Γ]^{n+1}. In the function-field case the units and class group must be those of the complete curve C_K (constant units, Pic(C_K)), because O_K^× is not F_{q^r}^× for totally real K with Γ ≠ 1 (source issue E15 here).

Proposition 3.22: G_{K,p} has Property E for pro-p Γ-groups (Theorem 2.5 with RG.1/property-e-at-level (c)), so R = ker ϖ = [Y(R)] by RG.1/property-e-criterion and (R/R*)^Γ = 0; the surjection of Lemma 3.17 then factors through (F_p[Γ]/(Σg))^{n+1} → R/R*, which is Γ-generated by Y-coordinates of n + 1 elements; lift them to S ⊆ R (generation theory: elements generate R as a closed normal subgroup iff their images generate R/R*, ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 5).
acceptance: For Γ = Z/2, Q = Q and p odd with K real quadratic, the 3-class tower group of K is a quotient of (𝓕_n)_3 ≅ the free pro-3 group of rank n (σ inverting the generators) by n + 1 Y-relations.
The conclusion is about the shape of G_{K,p}; it does not assert that G_{K,p} is finite.

Record that conjugacy of complements in the finite and profinite Schur–Zassenhaus theorem holds without further input when the normal subgroup or the quotient is (pro)solvable, and in general rests on the Feit–Thompson theorem; state the conjugacy half with that hypothesis (or an imported Feit–Thompson) so that consumers can track it. The supernatural order TauCeti.profiniteOrder and its behaviour under closed subgroups, quotients and finite products, to define pro-n′ Γ-groups.

The free pro-C group on a finite set for C the (extension-closed) class of finite groups of order prime to a fixed integer, with its universal property and functoriality in the generating set (so that a permutation of the basis induces an automorphism); and the free pro-p group on a finite set. Tau Ceti's main branch has TauCeti.freeProC; the pinned commit f790474 does not.
The lower p-central series (pLowerCentralSeries), the Frattini subgroup and generator rank d(G) = dim G/Φ(G), and Gaschütz lifting of generating tuples for pro-p groups.

Presentations of finitely generated pro-p groups: H²(F, F_p) = 0 for free pro-p F; for 1 → R → F → G → 1, elements of R generate it as a closed normal subgroup iff their images generate R/R^p[R, F], which is dual to H¹(R, F_p)^F; and r(G) = dim H²(G, F_p) for finite p-groups, with dim R/R^p[R, F] = r(G) + rank F − d(G).

The five-term inflation–restriction exact sequence 0 → H¹(G/N) → H¹(G) → H¹(N)^G → H²(G/N) → H²(G) for a closed normal subgroup N of a profinite group with F_p-coefficients, natural with respect to a finite group acting compatibly on G and N.

(a) Koch, Galois Theory of p-Extensions, Theorem 11.3 for S = ∅: for a number field K and the Galois group G̃ of its maximal unramified pro-p extension, an injection H²(G̃, F_p) ↪ (V/K^{×p})^∨ with V = {α ∈ K^× : (α) = 𝔞^p}, equivariant for automorphisms of K; and its function-field analogue for the complete curve. (b) Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, Corollary 8.7.3: for K/Q Galois with group Γ, K totally real, p ∤ |Γ| and μ_p ⊄ K, an F_p[Γ]-injection O_K^×/O_K^{×p} ↪ F_p[Γ]/(Σ_g g).

For a number field K, the Galois group of the maximal unramified abelian extension in which every infinite place splits completely is Cl(O_K) (the Hilbert class field), equivariantly for automorphisms of K over Q.

For a finite extension K/F_q(t) with O_K the integral closure of F_q[t], the Galois group of the maximal unramified abelian extension split completely above ∞ is Cl(O_K), and the maximal unramified abelian extension corresponds to Pic(C_K) (C_K the complete curve), equivariantly for automorphisms over F_q(t).

gaps.title: Conjugacy of coprime complements for non-solvable Γ (the Feit–Thompson theorem)
gaps.detail: Every statement from RG.0/sections-and-y onward carries the hypothesis (SZ_Γ) of RG.0/coprime-conjugacy-hypothesis. It is proved here for solvable Γ (which covers every Γ in the tests: Z/2, Z/4, (Z/2)², D_8, S_3) and for abelian kernels, and in general it is equivalent to the conjugacy half of the Schur–Zassenhaus theorem, whose proof for arbitrary coprime orders uses the Feit–Thompson odd-order theorem. Neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti at the pins has Feit–Thompson, and no atlas layer plans it (Tau Ceti's CFSGStatement roadmap does not state it). The same gap is recorded by ArithmeticStatistics ST.5 for LWZB Lemma 9.3 and Theorem 1.4. Owner: a foundational finite-group-theory roadmap; once it exists, (SZ_Γ) becomes a theorem for every finite Γ and the hypothesis can be dropped from the statements here.
